      "body": "Work package 4 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi. The runner checks the pin with require_pi, confirms by `pi --help` in a\nscratch home that the extension's flag is listed, and refuses otherwise,\nremoving what it made. It hands over no key and sets no agent directory: Pi\nsigns in from the maintainer's own ~/.pi/agent (Q-6). A prompt that starts with\n@ is refused, because Pi would read it as a file name.\n\nThe seven OpenCode-only functions, AGENT and GUARDED are gone. The tests get a\npi stand-in beside codex and osascript, and an opencode stand-in that must\nnever be called; the 25 canned effective-policy answers are replaced by tests of\nthe version pin, the read-back, the @ prompt, the scratch home and the absence\nof a key. 19 planted faults in the runner all turn a test red.\n\nDocuments that describe the verb to a reader still say OpenCode until package 5.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "171fb2185a25edcf71d8281f0eb4d3c2626eccc7",

    "1b731e4be82aed7d0bd4581e37955ca0492bbcfc": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-18T18:36:12Z",
      "body": "The status line, the session-start entry, the handover safety net, the\nparallel-session warning and the /uebergabe skill lived only in ~/.claude on\none machine. They now live in tools/claude-code/, with install.sh to put them\ninto ~/.claude (merging settings.json rather than replacing it) and --check to\nshow where ~/.claude has drifted from this directory.\n\nThe entry follows this repository's own rules for session continuity: the\nhandover is the newest file under docs/journal/handover/ (or journal/ in\nlakeswitch), its next step is shown at start, and the working tree is\nmeasured, not recalled. The automatic Haiku note is only a safety net for a\nsession that ended without a handover, and is shown as such.\n\nAGENTS.md gains \"Sessions across checkouts\": warn before changing files when\nanother session shares the checkout, \"not read\" is never \"none\", standing\nrules belong in a repository's AGENTS.md, and where the display lives. It sits\naway from the section draft PR #8 adds, so the two merge independently.\n\ntools/ is already classified as `bestand` in scripts/kit/manifest.yaml, so the\ndisplay stays here and does not travel with the kit.\n\nTested 2026-09-18: install into an empty home keeps unrelated settings, a\nsecond install adds nothing, a file changed only in ~/.claude is reported and\nkept as .bak; --check against the maintainer's ~/.claude is in sync. Test\nsuite: 64 failed, 183 passed, 4 skipped — identical on origin/main (9621e05),\nso this change adds no failure.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01X1cBmbhjDcegiYmf4TN5rA\n",

      "body": "The repair attempts of row F6-1 removed the direct launch of plain gate\ncommands from `_gate_argv` (decisions.md Q-9), so the world's own gates\n`make verify` and `bash scripts/verify_all.sh --job docs` now start as\n`sh -c <command>`.     "30bf06b4f8c96d6465f61a2c2dc84550741f163d": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-15T10:50:12Z",
      "body": "The scheduler selected its gates before it measured the baseline, both at the\nstart and in the refresh inside the admission. A gate list that gained a\nblocking gate between the two ran as the old selection while every later\nsnapshot matched, and the run ended green. Now the selection is read again\nright after the baseline snapshot, and the refresh measures its baseline\nbefore it reloads the list; a later change moves the tree and is refused or\nrefreshed. A seconds-only run still takes no snapshot.\n\nTests, red before the fix (tests/test_verify_before_admission.py):\n- test_selection_is_bound_to_the_measured_configuration\n- test_refreshed_selection_is_bound_to_the_measured_configuration\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "30bf06b4f8c96d6465f61a2c2dc84550741f163d",
      "subject": "fix(verify-cheap-before-admission): the gate selection is bound to the measured configuration (phase-6 row F6-2)",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/verify_run.py"
      ]
    },

      "author_utc": "2026-11-14T18:59:01Z",
      "body": "The tree baseline is measured only for a run with protected work - the one\ncase that reuses cheap results across the admission. A seconds-only job\n(docs, drift) and a cheap pass that ended blocking red rely on no baseline,\nso they no longer refuse over an unmeasurable or moving tree (L2-3, L2-8).\nEvery ending - green, red, refused, refused admission - goes through one\nfinish(): the refused run names the gates it did not run, prints a banner\nand closes its history record red (L2-2). The cheap phase's not-run header\nnames every blocking red gate instead of claiming a stop at the first\n(L2-7). A refusal names the paths that moved. The worker rule lives once in\nverify_run.worker_bound, used by the full and the targeted check (L2-6).\nThe gates' default interpreter comes from the env argument (L2-9).\n\nL2-1 is rejected: ruff and pytest self-ignore their caches; the new proof\ntest_real_tool_caches_keep_the_baseline_stable runs both inside a checkout\nwithout user-level excludes and stays stable.\n\nOrchestrator hand edit (Opus subagent, maintainer's word of 2026-11-14).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,

    "7533598324c2aa390330623901d9d7e9f1609b6d": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-15T10:52:50Z",
      "body": "A SIGTERM after `Popen` created the gate but before its process group was\nregistered raised `GateInterrupted` before the cleanup existed, so the gate\nkept running and could keep the admission descriptor. `gate_process` now\nholds the run's signals back with temporary handlers (never\n`pthread_sigmask`, whose mask the child would inherit) from before `Popen`\nuntil inside the `try` whose `finally` ends the group, then delivers them;\nthe reader start sits inside that `try` too, and a reader that never started\nhas its pipe closed instead of joined.\n\nTest, red before the fix:\ntests/test_verify_before_admission.py::test_a_signal_at_the_launch_boundary_still_ends_the_gate\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "7533598324c2aa390330623901d9d7e9f1609b6d",
      "subject": "fix(verify-cheap-before-admission): a signal at the gate's launch boundary is deferred (phase-6 row F6-3)",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/verify_run.py"
      ]
    },

      "body": "Phase-6 round-13 rows F-56 and F-57 (bead coding-harness-icw).\n\n- given_neighbours refuses a research header that states\n  neighbours: more than once (exit 2, before any call) (F-56).\n- dispatch waits for its workers through a completion semaphore, not\n  Thread.join: CPython 3.12 marks a thread stopped when an interrupt\n  lands in join. On an interrupt it sets the stop event, waits a\n  bounded time for every worker to reap its child, then re-raises (F-57).\n\nRepair by Sonnet 5.5 (runner attempt, then a sub-agent with the\norchestrator's join diagnosis). The orchestrator changed the F-57\ntest to a real SIGINT, checked red first by hand against a711d08 and\nran make verify green (21:39:00Z-21:49:09Z, 3110 passed, 16 skipped).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

    "82a013b92bfab78830cdeeb982d597e217216c64": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-20T11:20:58Z",
      "body": "Main brings the shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py, PR #416,\nbead coding-harness-bxxt.6), venv_guard (PR #415) and the journal citation\ngate (PR #418). The slip counter (bead coding-harness-bxxt.7) is carried into\nmain's structure; nothing of either side is reverted.\n\nConflict resolutions:\n\n- scripts/verify_duration.py: main's in-process writers stay (record_start,\n  record_gate, record_end with root, state_root and env). The slip counter's\n  comparison evidence is attached to them: record_start records\n  common_git_dir for its root, reads the runner-owned comparison variables\n  from the scheduler's env (_comparison_fields(env), falling back to the\n  process environment for the CLI), and creates the targeted history beside\n  the duration history under the same state root at the first version-2\n  marker. append_event/_open_history take both the slip counter's\n  `destination` (the targeted history) and main's keyword `state_root`;\n  targeted_history_path accepts a state root too. Imports keep both\n  Sequence and dataclass/field; _git and _gate_file_digest take main's form.\n  New COMPARISON_ENV_NAMES lists the three variables.\n- scripts/stage2.py: main's scheduler path stays the one full check. The\n  slip counter's single entry point full_verify(root, env, key, change,\n  prepare) is kept, now built on main's body: prepare runs first, outside\n  any admission (main's intent for the full-mode attempt), then\n  intent-to-add, then _scheduled_verify with\n  verify_duration.full_run_context(_checked_tree(root, change), change)\n  added to the scheduler's environment. verify_attempt's full mode hands its\n  preparation (format, cheap checks, ledger clearing, prepare_derived) to\n  full_verify as `prepare` instead of duplicating the intent-to-add,\n  scheduler and cleanup block (house rule 9: one path).\n- scripts/verify_run.py (no conflict, one addition): after recording the\n  start, run_verification drops the comparison variables from the gates'\n  environment, so a gate never inherits them and a check a gate starts is\n  never recorded as a second full run of the same change and tree.\n- tests/test_stage2.py: both sides' new tests kept. The slip end-to-end test\n  now uses the world's committed gate list instead of creating its own\n  decisions/ folder, and its `make` stub is the scheduler's protected gate:\n  it records nothing (the scheduler records start, gate and end) and fails if\n  it inherits the comparison context.\n- tests/test_verify_duration.py: the slip counter's version of the\n  derived-never-persisted test (the reader `slips` is exposed) replaces\n  main's deferral assertions; main's criterion-8 completion-context test is\n  kept.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",
      "body_truncated": false,

    "942c683f3dc1b50a91ace30a1c79d3927f80f9b3": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-29T08:29:43Z",
      "body": "Omnigent's own tools reach a Claude Code session as mcp__omnigent__<tool>,\nand neither Claude Code's path rules nor the hooks on its file tools see\nthem. scripts/omnigent_policy.py now holds the one list (27 denied tools,\n17 allowed, the protected config path, a reason for each) and renders both\nlayers from it:\n\n- layer 1: permissions.deny in .claude/settings.json, one exact rule per\n  denied tool plus Edit(//**/.omnigent/config.yaml). It holds alone.\n- layer 2: tools/omnigent/policy.yaml, an Omnigent default policy with two\n  CEL policies, and tools/omnigent/install.sh, which merges it into the\n  maintainer's Omnigent config (backup, validation with Omnigent's own\n  parser, refuses without a terminal). It is built, not installed.\n\nThe CEL policy tests `in` over a literal list rather than `.exists(...)`:\ncelpy evaluates both sides of `&&`, and on an event without a tool name the\nmacro's chain of errors doubles its message at every element, which hangs\nthe evaluation at 27 tools. The offline tests run every odd event shape\nthrough Omnigent's cel_policy under a time limit.\n\nThe script has no CI caller by nature (the installer runs on the\nmaintainer's machine), so it is listed in ci_gates.OHNE_AUFRUFER.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HRfJHTtj6rvcgudkYjJoP7\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "942c683f3dc1b50a91ace30a1c79d3927f80f9b3",

      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/ci_gates.py",
        "scripts/omnigent_policy.py"
      ]
    },

      "body": "install.sh took the launcher's first line literally after \"#!\", so\n\"#!/usr/bin/env python3\" was rejected as \"Omnigent not found\", while\nscripts/omnigent_policy.py handled the env form.       "author_utc": "2026-11-13T23:38:23Z",
      "body": "The shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py) behind\nscripts/verify_all.sh and Stage 2: every unprotected (seconds) gate runs\nbefore admission and all red ones are reported together; only protected\ngates (cost minutes, or needs_admission) run under one admission; an\nunchanged tree reuses the cheap results, a changed one reruns them.\n\nOrchestrator hand implementation after three rejected runner attempts (two\npost-run checks red, the third model call ended with exit 1), approved by\nthe maintainer on 2026-11-13. Built on the tree of implement attempt 3\n(refs/stage2/attempts/verify-cheap-before-admission/implement-attempt-3-\n20261113T221950681498Z), with these repairs:\n\n- verify_run: no empty not-run header when the last gate was the stop.\n- verify_all.sh: keeps the duration_admission_context boundary, so an\n  ancestor's admission context is dropped and a nested run records reuse;\n  the attempt had removed it and its test block, both restored unchanged.\n- test fixtures: markers outside the measured tree, the release marker of\n  the nested proof reset, fake_git accepts the checkout argument.\n\nExisting tests changed because the spec changes the behaviour they pin:\n- tests/test_ci.py timing test (A): the start record is written before any\n  admission, so its admission_reused is unknown (None); the completion\n  record carries admission_requested False and no context. (B): the stop\n  at the first blocking gate is now proved among minutes gates, since the\n  cheap phase runs through every seconds gate (decisions Q-3).\n- the attempt's other changes to tests/test_ci.py, test_verify_cheap_first,\n  test_gate_catalog and test_stage2 (cost classes in fixtures, a git HEAD\n  for the tree measurement, the admission column, no whole-run admission\n  for the seconds-only document subset) follow the same spec criteria 2,\n  3, 5 and 10.\n\nChecked: ruff check and format clean over scripts/ and tests/; the new and\ndirectly touched test files 105 passed; tests/test_ci.py 179 passed,\n2 skipped.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

Each slot ends with exactly one terminal outcome.\n\n    ``on_terminal(slot, result)`` is called once per slot, in the thread that set the outcome and\n    before that thread takes its next slot (launched, cancelled, refused and not-started slots\n    alike). An exception from it, or from ``audit`` carrying a ``stage_stop_reason`` attribute,\n    is a stage stop without a security refusal: queued slots are cancelled, running children\n    are stopped and reaped with their output kept, no further callback runs (the store it\n    writes to is the thing that failed) and the exit code is 1 unless a security refusal makes\n    it 2. The dispatcher knows nothing about what the callbacks write.\n    \"\"\"\n    stop = stop if stop is not None else threading.Event()\n    ordered = sorted(slots, key=lambda s: (not s.required, s.order))\n    queues: dict[str, deque] = {}\n    for slot in ordered:\n        queues.setdefault(slot.provider, deque()).append(slot)\n    gate_lock = threading.Lock()\n    results: dict[str, SlotResult] = {}\n    sequence: list[str] = []\n    security = threading.Event()\n    failure: list = []  # the first (reason, detail) of a failed callback\n    pending = threading.local()\n\n    def finish(slot, outcome, *, started=False, rc=None, out=\"\", err=\"\", record=None, allowance=None):\n        results[slot.slot_id] = SlotResult(\n            slot.slot_id, dict(slot.identity), slot.required, outcome, started, rc, out, err, record, allowance\n        )\n        if not hasattr(pending, \"slots\"):\n            pending.slots = []\n        pending.slots.append(slot)\n\n    failure_lock = threading.Lock()\n    reported: set[str] = set()\n\n    def stage_stop(exc):\n        with failure_lock:\n            if not failure:\n                reason = getattr(exc, \"stage_stop_reason\", None) or \"state-store-unwritable\"\n                failure.append((reason, f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\"))\n        stop.set()\n\n    def report_terminal():\n        \"\"\"Run the callback for each outcome this thread just set, before it takes another slot.\"\"\"\n        slots, pending.slots = getattr(pending, \"slots\", []), []\n        for slot in slots:\n            if slot.slot_id in reported:\n                continue\n            reported.add(slot.slot_id)\n            if on_terminal is None or failure:\n                continue\n            try:\n                on_terminal(slot, results[slot.slot_id])\n            except Exception as exc:\n                stage_stop(exc)\n\n    def remaining():\n        return None if deadline is None else deadline - reserve - clock()\n\n    def out_of_time():\n        left = remaining()\n        return left is not None and left <= 0\n\n    def launch_next(queue):\n        \"\"\"Pop, gate, audit and launch under the one lock; return (slot, proc, allowance) or None.\"\"\"\n        with gate_lock:\n            if not queue:\n                return \"done\"\n            # Required-first holds across providers (F-54): a free slot waits until every\n            # required slot of every provider has been taken from its queue.\n            if not queue[0].required and any(q and q[0].required for q in queues.values()):\n                return \"wait\"\n            slot = queue.popleft()\n            sequence.append(slot.slot_id)\n            if stop.is_set():\n                finish(slot, \"cancelled\")\n                return None\n            if out_of_time():\n                finish(slot, \"not-started-deadline\")\n                return None\n            try:\n                verdict = gate(slot)\n           ",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "def hold_admission(command: list[str]) -> Iterator[tuple[int, ...] | None]:\n    \"\"\"One machine admission around protected work: queue, memory gate, published ownership.\n\n    Yields the descriptors local children must inherit, or None when this\n    entry is nested in an ancestor's admission. A process that already holds\n    or is acquiring an independent admission is refused before any queueing.\n    Refusals raise VerifyLockRefused or MemoryFloorRefused before the body\n    runs; release happens in every ending, after any child cleanup the caller\n    does.\n    \"\"\"\n    inherited = nested_holder_pid()\n    if inherited is not None:\n        _log(f\"inheriting admission from pid {inherited}; no queue and no memory wait\")\n        yield None\n        return\n    with _independent_admission_guard():\n        setting = verify_slots_setting()\n        admission = _Admission(_prepare_state(), command, setting)\n        try:\n            admission.enter()\n        except BaseException:\n            admission.release()\n            raise\n        try:\n            yield admission.pass_fds()\n        finally:\n            admission.release()\n",

          "excerpt": "def inherit_env(env: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The environment a local check runs under, with the admission state it must carry.\n\n    This is additive and local-only: a runner's allowlist stays closed, foreign\n    calls receive none of these names, and a genuine inherited marker travels\n    so a nested check reuses its ancestor's admission even after local\n    environment filtering.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = dict(env)\n    env[\"XDG_STATE_HOME\"] = str(state_base())\n    if FLOOR_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[FLOOR_ENV] = os.environ[FLOOR_ENV]\n    # The slot setting travels to local children when present, so a nested\n    # runner's own protected work — never a nested entry, which parses\n    # nothing — sees the same configuration its parent had (criterion 2).\n    # The foreign-model environment allowlist stays closed to HARNESS_*.\n    if SLOTS_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[SLOTS_ENV] = os.environ[SLOTS_ENV]\n    nested = nested_holder_pid()\n    marker, token = (nested, os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV)) if nested is not None else (_active_pid(), _active_token())\n    if marker is not None and token:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(marker)\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = token\n    else:\n        env.pop(LOCK_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(TOKEN_ENV, None)\n    # The admission context resolves the same way the child itself would: its\n    # own active admission, an inherited one, or nothing (bead\n    # coding-harness-1um6). A fresh context travels so the child records the\n    # measured wait as its own; an inherited one does not travel — the child\n    # resolves the shared context from the validated ownership record instead.\n    # Never the token.\n    context = admission_context()\n    if context.admission_id is not None and context.reused is False:\n        env[ADMISSION_ID_ENV] = context.admission_id\n        if context.wait_seconds is not None:\n            env[ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV] = repr(context.wait_seconds)\n    else:\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_ID_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV, None)\n    return env\n",

          "excerpt": "def state_base() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"The state base the shared root hangs off; an inheriting child must keep this, not the root.\n\n    A child handed `XDG_STATE_HOME` pointing at the root itself would resolve\n    the next layer down (`.../coding-harness/coding-harness`) and read another\n    machine's state — so the environment a local child inherits names the base,\n    and both sides resolve the same root.\n    \"\"\"\n    base = os.environ.get(\"XDG_STATE_HOME\")\n    # A relative value is ignored, as the XDG base-directory rule says: it would resolve against each\n    # entry's own working directory and split the shared admission (review row L1-3).\n    return Path(base) if base and Path(base).is_absolute() else Path.home() / \".local\" / \"state\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def _own_group(proc):\n    \"\"\"Find the child's own process group, including descendants of an already reaped leader.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        return os.getpgid(proc.pid) == proc.pid and proc.pid != os.getpgrp()\n    except ProcessLookupError:\n        # The leader may already have been reaped while descendants retain its PGID.\n        # A live group with this id cannot be reassigned to a different leader.\n        if proc.pid != os.getpgrp():\n            try:\n                os.killpg(proc.pid, 0)\n                return True\n            except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):\n                pass\n        return False\n    except PermissionError:\n        return False\n",

          "excerpt": "def _stop_and_reap(proc, grace):\n    \"\"\"Terminate the child (its whole group when it has one), kill after the grace, reap.\"\"\"\n    group = _own_group(proc)\n    _signal_child(proc, signal.SIGTERM, group)\n    leader_exited = True\n    try:\n        proc.wait(timeout=grace)\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n        leader_exited = False\n    # After the grace the whole launched group is killed, also when the leader already exited on\n    # SIGTERM: a descendant that ignores SIGTERM must not outlive a cancellation (F-34). A group\n    # with no member left makes the call a no-op.\n    if group or not leader_exited:\n        _signal_child(proc, signal.SIGKILL, group)\n    if not leader_exited:\n        try:\n            proc.wait(timeout=max(grace, 5.0))\n        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:  # pragma: no cover - SIGKILL was sent to a live child\n            return \"\", \"\"\n    try:\n        return proc.communicate(timeout=max(grace, 1.0))\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n        return \"\", \"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def dispatch(\n    slots,\n    *,\n    gate: Callable[[Slot], GateVerdict],\n    launcher: Callable[[Slot, float], Any],\n    audit: Callable[[Slot, GateVerdict], None] | None = None,\n    on_terminal: Callable[[Slot, SlotResult], None] | None = None,\n    stop: threading.Event | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    reserve: float = 0.0,\n    clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,\n    per_provider_limit: int = PER_PROVIDER_LIMIT,\n    grace: float = 2.0,\n) -> DispatchResult:\n    \"\"\"Run one stage. Each slot ends with exactly one terminal outcome.\n\n    ``on_terminal(slot, result)`` is called once per slot, in the thread that set the outcome and\n    before that thread takes its next slot (launched, cancelled, refused and not-started slots\n    alike). An exception from it, or from ``audit`` carrying a ``stage_stop_reason`` attribute,\n    is a stage stop without a security refusal: queued slots are cancelled, running children\n    are stopped and reaped with their output kept, no further callback runs (the store it\n    writes to is the thing that failed) and the exit code is 1 unless a security refusal makes\n    it 2. The dispatcher knows nothing about what the callbacks write.\n    \"\"\"\n    stop = stop if stop is not None else threading.Event()\n    ordered = sorted(slots, key=lambda s: (not s.required, s.order))\n    queues: dict[str, deque] = {}\n    for slot in ordered:\n        queues.setdefault(slot.provider, deque()).append(slot)\n    gate_lock = threading.Lock()\n    results: dict[str, SlotResult] = {}\n    sequence: list[str] = []\n    security = threading.Event()\n    failure: list = []  # the first (reason, detail) of a failed callback\n    pending = threading.local()\n\n    def finish(slot, outcome, *, started=False, rc=None, out=\"\", err=\"\", record=None, allowance=None):\n        results[slot.slot_id] = SlotResult(\n            slot.slot_id, dict(slot.identity), slot.required, outcome, started, rc, out, err, record, allowance\n        )\n        if not hasattr(pending, \"slots\"):\n            pending.slots = []\n        pending.slots.append(slot)\n\n    failure_lock = threading.Lock()\n    reported: set[str] = set()\n\n    def stage_stop(exc):\n        with failure_lock:\n            if not failure:\n                reason = getattr(exc, \"stage_stop_reason\", None) or \"state-store-unwritable\"\n     ",

          "excerpt": "def launch(\n    command: list[str],\n    root: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str],\n    secret: str | list[str] | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    pass_fds: tuple[int, ...] = (),\n) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    \"\"\"Start a foreign program: empty standard input, the worktree as its directory.\n\n    With a `timeout` the program leads a process group of its own, and a timeout kills the whole\n    group: a hung `make verify` leaves no shell, pytest or worker behind to write into the worktree\n    after the run stopped (O188-4 of the #188 review). The group is registered while it runs, so an\n    interrupted runner kills it too (`kill_live`), and the drain after a kill is bounded by\n    `KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS`: a descendant that left the group is abandoned, not waited for.\n    `pass_fds` hands descriptors — a verification admission's lock — to the child, so ownership\n    outlives this process for exactly as long as the child and its own children run.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        if timeout is None and deadline is None:\n            return subprocess.run(\n                command,\n                cwd=root,\n                env=env,\n                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                capture_output=True,\n                text=True,\n                errors=\"replace\",\n                check=False,\n                pass_fds=pass_fds,\n            )\n        process = None\n        try:\n            with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                    raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted; no program starts\")\n                with defer_launch_signals():\n                    # Admission and waiting for the launch lock use the same round budget.\n                    # Recheck at process creation so a late replacement is never consumed.\n                    if deadline is not None:\n                        left = remaining(deadline)\n                        timeout = left if timeout is None else min(timeout, left)\n                    process = subprocess.Popen(\n                        command,\n                        cwd=root,\n                        env=env,\n                        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        text=True,\n                        errors=\"replace\",\n                        start_new_session=True,\n                        pass_fds=pass_fds,\n                    )\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.add(process.pid)\n            # Cancellation may have arrived while Popen was starting in a worker.\n            if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted during launch\")\n            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)\n            # A grandchild that kept running after the command exited would outlive an admission\n            # released around this call; the group is ended before returning (review row F6-5).\n            verify_lock.end_lingering_group(process.pid)\n        except BaseException:\n            if process is None:\n                raise\n            # Kill before unregistering and before any Popen cleanup could wait for a live child.\n            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)\n            with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):\n                process.communicate(timeout=KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS)\n            raise\n        finally:\n            if process is not None:\n                for pipe in (process.stdout, process.stderr):\n                    if pipe is not None:\n                        pipe.close()\n                with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.discard(process.pid)\n        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:\n        what = limit or f\"the reviewer time limit after {REVIEWER_MINUTES:",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::Sessions across checkouts",
          "end_line": 190,
          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair.           "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5).           "excerpt": "## Night runs (unattended)\n\nFor an unattended session the same install provides the night profile:\n`night.py` and its settings fragment `night-settings.json`. A process that already holds\n    or is acquiring an independent admission is refused before any queueing.\n    Refusals raise VerifyLockRefused or MemoryFloorRefused before the body\n    runs; release happens in every ending, after any child cleanup the caller\n    does.\n    \"\"\"\n    inherited = nested_holder_pid()\n    if inherited is not None:\n        _log(f\"inheriting admission from pid {inherited}; no queue and no memory wait\")\n        yield None\n        return\n    with _independent_admission_guard():\n        setting = verify_slots_setting()\n        admission = _Admission(_prepare_state(), command, setting)\n        try:\n            admission.enter()\n        except BaseException:\n            admission.release()\n            raise\n        try:\n            yield admission.pass_fds()\n        finally:\n            admission.release()\n",

          "excerpt": "def inherit_env(env: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The environment a local check runs under, with the admission state it must carry.\n\n    This is additive and local-only: a runner's allowlist stays closed, foreign\n    calls receive none of these names, and a genuine inherited marker travels\n    so a nested check reuses its ancestor's admission even after local\n    environment filtering.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = dict(env)\n    env[\"XDG_STATE_HOME\"] = str(state_base())\n    if FLOOR_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[FLOOR_ENV] = os.environ[FLOOR_ENV]\n    # The slot setting travels to local children when present, so a nested\n    # runner's own protected work — never a nested entry, which parses\n    # nothing — sees the same configuration its parent had (criterion 2).\n    # The foreign-model environment allowlist stays closed to HARNESS_*.\n    if SLOTS_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[SLOTS_ENV] = os.environ[SLOTS_ENV]\n    nested = nested_holder_pid()\n    marker, token = (nested, os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV)) if nested is not None else (_active_pid(), _active_token())\n    if marker is not None and token:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(marker)\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = token\n    else:\n        env.pop(LOCK_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(TOKEN_ENV, None)\n    # The admission context resolves the same way the child itself would: its\n    # own active admission, an inherited one, or nothing (bead\n    # coding-harness-1um6). A fresh context travels so the child records the\n    # measured wait as its own; an inherited one does not travel — the child\n    # resolves the shared context from the validated ownership record instead.\n    # Never the token.\n    context = admission_context()\n    if context.admission_id is not None and context.reused is False:\n        env[ADMISSION_ID_ENV] = context.admission_id\n        if context.wait_seconds is not None:\n            env[ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV] = repr(context.wait_seconds)\n    else:\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_ID_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV, None)\n    return env\n",

          "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        elif not table:\n            raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        for line in table:\n            parts = line.split(None, 2)\n            if (\n                len(parts) != 3\n                or not parts[0].isdigit()\n                or not run_report.ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1])\n                or not parts[2].strip()\n            ):\n                raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        rows = run_report.parse_processes(raw, changes)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        lines.append(str(error))\n        return lines\n    if not rows:\n        if run_report.stage2 is not None:\n            lines.append(\"none matched\")\n        return lines\n    lines.extend(f\"pid {row.pid} · {row.label} · change {row.change} · elapsed {row.elapsed}\" for row in rows)\n    return lines\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_jobs_use_existing_process_recognition(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Fault: a real invocation is lost, a shell wrapper or a quoted command is counted as a job,\n    change attribution is guessed for an unknown change, runner recognition claims `none` when\n    its definitions are gone, or raw command arguments leak into the block (spec criterion 5).\"\"\"\n    worktree = tmp_path / \"repo\"\n    (worktree / \"plans\" / \"changes\" / \"night-machine-facts\").mkdir(parents=True)\n    proc = proc_fixture(tmp_path)\n\n    def block(run, root: Path) -> str:\n        return machine_facts.render(snapshot(run, fake_statvfs({root: statvfs_result(GIB)}), cwd=root, proc_dir=proc))\n\n    outputs = {\n        **git_keys(worktree),\n        (\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"): worktree_list_fixture(MAIN),\n        (\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"): PS_TABLE,\n    }\n    out = block(fake_run(outputs), worktree)\n    job_lines = [line for line in out.splitlines() if line.lstrip().startswith(\"pid \")]\n    assert len(job_lines) == 2  # the implement invocation and `make verify`; wrapper, editor and echo are not jobs\n    assert \"pid 12345 · implement · change night-machine-facts · elapsed 03:12\" in out\n    assert \"pid 12347 · verify · change not read · elapsed 12:00\" in out\n    assert \"--route\" not in out and \"flash\" not in out  # raw arguments never print\n    assert \"zsh\" not in out and \"echo\" not in out and \"Editor\" not in out  # non-jobs never print\n\n    # An unknown change is never guessed into a name.\n    outputs = {\n        **git_keys(worktree),\n        (\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"): ps_output(\"12350 05:00 python3 scripts/stage2.py implement not-a-change\"),\n    }\n    assert \"pid 12350 · implement · change not read · ela",

          "excerpt": "def test_launcher_forces_noninteractive_permissions(workspace: SimpleNamespace) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 2, test half: the launched call and the overlay leave no interactive permission wait.\"\"\"\n    write_settings(\n        user_settings(workspace),\n        {\"statusLine\": {\"type\": \"command\"}, \"permissions\": {\"ask\": [ASK_RULE], \"deny\": [DENY_RULE]}},\n    )\n    write_settings(local_settings(workspace), {\"permissions\": {\"deny\": [\"Bash(rm -rf /)\"]}})\n    passthrough = [\"-p\", \"night work\", \"--model\", \"sonnet\"]\n    done = run_night(workspace, *passthrough)\n    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stderr\n    argv = launched_argv(workspace)\n    assert argv[0] == \"--settings\" and Path(argv[1]).name == \"settings.json\"\n    assert argv[2:4] == [\"--permission-mode\", \"dontAsk\"]\n    assert argv[4:] == passthrough\n    overlay = recorded_overlay(workspace)\n    assert overlay[\"permissions\"][\"defaultMode\"] == \"dontAsk\"\n    assert \"ask\" not in overlay[\"permissions\"]\n    assert \"allow\" not in overlay[\"permissions\"], \"the night profile must not add blanket allows\"\n    deny = overlay[\"permissions\"][\"deny\"]\n    assert len(deny) == len(set(deny)), \"the overlay repeats a deny rule\"\n    assert set(deny) == {ASK_RULE, DENY_RULE, \"Bash(rm -rf /)\"}\n    assert set(overlay) == {\"permissions\"}, \"inherited non-permission settings must stay in their native layers\"\n    assert recorded(workspace, \".lifetime\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"True 0o700\"\n    assert not Path(argv[1]).exists(), \"the overlay outlived the child\"\n    assert not Path(argv[1]).parent.exists(), \"the private overlay directory outlived the child\"\n",

          "end_line": 147,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen: option (1), with the inference removed, the reverse direction held,\nand the whole gate carried by the kit with a day per repository — because an\nattribution per edit needs the claim where the edit is made, one rule is\neasier to hold than an explicit rule beside a guess, and a workflow rule that\nholds in one repository alone is not a rule of the workflow (Q-1 to Q-5).\n\n**What is decided**, in five points:\n\n1. A change claims, in the header of its own spec, every file under\n   `docs/adr/` it creates, changes or removes. A later change that amends an\n   ADR claims that amendment itself.\n2. An ADR edit belongs to the change of the measured work that claims it. A\n   change that does not claim the file is no owner of it, whatever else the\n   work touches. The owner owes five interview answers of the maintainer,\n   whatever its class and its date.\n3. An ADR edit that no change of the work claims is a finding that names the\n   remedy. Nothing infers an owner from the paths a diff touches or from an\n   ADR's text.\n4. For a feature begun after its repository adopted the gate, the answer \"yes\"\n   comes with at least one claimed ADR file, and the answer \"no\" with none.\n5. The interview gate travels with the kit as mechanism. Each repository\n   records the day it adopted the gate; a change begun on or before that day\n   is exempt from the class minimums and from point 4, never from points 2 and\n   3. Moving that day is a decision pull request.\n\n**How it holds from this change on:**\n\n* The claim is the spec header field `adr_files`; the gate\n  `interview-minimums` (`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`) holds points 2\n  to 4.\n* The day stands in `decisions/adoption.yaml`, a file that stays in its\n  repository; this repository's day is 2026-10-08, the day it adopted the\n  gate, so no change here moves between stock and subject. The gate reads the\n  day through `scripts/adoption.py`, which any other gate can call with its\n  own id (bead coding-harness-wpv); without the record the gate does not\n  measure (exit 3).\n* The gate script, its test, the reader and the reader's test travel as\n  mechanism (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`); the record stays as stock. An\n  instance such as LakeSwitch receives them with its next pinned Coding\n  Harness release (bead coding-harness-dj9).\n\n**What this record does not fix.** The field's name, the record's name and\nform, the reader and the gate's messages are the change's design: they change\nin an ordinary change as long as the five points hold.\n\nThis record amends no D- or O-number. It replaces the attribution of the\narchived change interview-minimums — the change folders a diff touches — and\nthe interim rule of pull request #126; ADR 0013 is unchanged.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "# ADR 0025 — A runner repair passes a targeted check; one full make verify precedes phase 6\n\n* Status: accepted by the merge of the pull request that carries this file.\n  Until that merge, open is proposed and closed is rejected. Amends ADR 0021\n  decision 6; supersedes no ADR. Amends no D- or O-number.\n* Review: the maintainer decided on 2026-11-08, in the conversation, that\n  ADR 0021 decision 6 changes together with the runner change that makes a\n  repair pass on a targeted check (pull request #343, bead\n  coding-harness-gxwg), and that the amendment travels in a decision pull\n  request of its own (answer \"Fertig machen + ADR-PR\"), and answered its\n  interview the same day (`plans/changes/adr-repair-check/decisions.md`,\n  Q-1 to Q-5). Decider: maintainer ·\n  prepared by Claude Code. Acceptance is the merge commit; the review header\n  remains pending.\n* Date: 2026-11-08 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nADR 0021 decision 6 ends \"requiring `make verify` green after repair as\ntoday\". Every runner repair therefore paid for a full `make verify`, even for\na narrow edit. Full checks run one at a time under the machine-wide verify\nadmission (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, \"One admission per user and machine\"), so a\nrepair cycle waits for the lock and then for the whole suite. The workflow\nrecords a full run at 12 to 13 minutes (measured 2026-10-30); the lane times\nthis decision should shorten are not measured.\n\nThe maintainer had already let a targeted check stand in for a full one after\na hand repair by the orchestrator (2026-10-30, bead coding-harness-24ag). The\nchange `repair-targeted-check` extends that rule to runner repairs and adds an\nenforced full check before phase 6 (`plans/changes/repair-targeted-check/`,\non the branch of #343). Without this amendment the ADR would contradict the\ngate the runner enforces (review-loop row L8-3 of that change; bead\ncoding-harness-firy).\n\n## Decision\n\nADR 0021 decision 6's last sentence is replaced by:\n\n1. After a runner repair the runner runs a targeted check: the tests linked\n   to the touched files, the prior retry selections, ruff on the touched\n   Python files, and the gates the touched file kinds feed.\n2. When that selection is not safe, the full `make verify` runs instead, as\n   the fallback for that repair.\n3. One fresh green full `make verify` on the head under review is required\n   before phase 6. A red, unstartable or timed-out run stops the review;\n   runner audit lines in `findings.md` do not count as a new head.\n4. The orchestrator measures repair duration, verify-lock wait and every\n   failure the full check before phase 6 finds that a targeted check missed,\n   over five changes or two weeks, whichever comes first, and reports the\n   result to the maintainer.\n5. This rule holds from the merge. The testing-strategy spike (bead\n   coding-harness-1ga5) may amend or replace it with an ADR of its own; the\n   measurement of point 4 enters that spike as a finding.\n\nThe rest of ADR 0021 decision 6 stands unchanged.\n\n## Consequences\n\n* A repair cycle no longer waits for a full run unless its selection is\n  unsafe; the effect on cycle and lane times is not yet measured.\n* A targeted check can miss a test the touch map does not link to a touched\n  file.           "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008).           "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(not for a spike)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | a current review of the spec, no open `[AMBIGUITY]`; at most three spec-review rounds — the final draft after round three needs no new review, a fourth round only by a recorded maintainer answer |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one.           "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

Decider: maintainer ·\n  prepared by Claude Code. Acceptance is the merge commit; the review header\n  remains pending.\n* Date: 2026-11-08 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nADR 0021 decision 6 ends \"requiring `make verify` green after repair as\ntoday\". Every runner repair therefore paid for a full `make verify`, even for\na narrow edit. Full checks run one at a time under the machine-wide verify\nadmission (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, \"One admission per user and machine\"), so a\nrepair cycle waits for the lock and then for the whole suite. The workflow\nrecords a full run at 12 to 13 minutes (measured 2026-10-30); the lane times\nthis decision should shorten are not measured.\n\nThe maintainer had already let a targeted check stand in for a full one after\na hand repair by the orchestrator (2026-10-30, bead coding-harness-24ag). The\nchange `repair-targeted-check` extends that rule to runner repairs and adds an\nenforced full check before phase 6 (`plans/changes/repair-targeted-check/`,\non the branch of #343). Without this amendment the ADR would contradict the\ngate the runner enforces (review-loop row L8-3 of that change; bead\ncoding-harness-firy).\n\n## Decision\n\nADR 0021 decision 6's last sentence is replaced by:\n\n1. After a runner repair the runner runs a targeted check: the tests linked\n   to the touched files, the prior retry selections, ruff on the touched\n   Python files, and the gates the touched file kinds feed.\n2. When that selection is not safe, the full `make verify` runs instead, as\n   the fallback for that repair.\n3. One fresh green full `make verify` on the head under review is required\n   before phase 6. A red, unstartable or timed-out run stops the review;\n   runner audit lines in `findings.md` do not count as a new head.\n4. The orchestrator measures repair duration, verify-lock wait and every\n   failure the full check before phase 6 finds that a targeted check missed,\n   over five changes or two weeks, whichever comes first, and reports the\n   result to the maintainer.\n5. This rule holds from the merge. The testing-strategy spike (bead\n   coding-harness-1ga5) may amend or replace it with an ADR of its own; the\n   measurement of point 4 enters that spike as a finding.\n\nThe rest of ADR 0021 decision 6 stands unchanged.\n\n## Consequences\n\n* A repair cycle no longer waits for a full run unless its selection is\n  unsafe; the effect on cycle and lane times is not yet measured.\n* A targeted check can miss a test the touch map does not link to a touched\n  file. The full `make verify` before phase 6 catches such a miss before the\n  review, and CI remains the full gate of the pull request.\n* A repair can be marked fixed on a targeted result that the full check\n  later turns red; that red stops phase 6 until it is repaired.\n\n## Validation\n\n* #343 carries the runner implementation and its criterion tests; this\n  pull request carries only the ADR text.\n* CI on this pull request is its gate; merge, not this draft, accepts the ADR.\n\n## Implement and draft amendment — the targeted check covers more verbs, 2026-11-12\n\nThe maintainer answered the interview of the change\n`targeted-check-more-verbs` on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12\n(`plans/changes/targeted-check-more-verbs/decisions.md`, Q-1 to Q-6; bead\ncoding-harne",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 93,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::Sessions across checkouts",
          "end_line": 190,
          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair. Reason: a run's history cannot be reset, and asking each time stopped\n  lanes overnight.\n\n",
