          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008).           "excerpt": "def launch(\n    command: list[str],\n    root: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str],\n    secret: str | list[str] | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    pass_fds: tuple[int, ...] = (),\n) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    \"\"\"Start a foreign program: empty standard input, the worktree as its directory.\n\n    With a `timeout` the program leads a process group of its own, and a timeout kills the whole\n    group: a hung `make verify` leaves no shell, pytest or worker behind to write into the worktree\n    after the run stopped (O188-4 of the #188 review). The group is registered while it runs, so an\n    interrupted runner kills it too (`kill_live`), and the drain after a kill is bounded by\n    `KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS`: a descendant that left the group is abandoned, not waited for.\n    `pass_fds` hands descriptors — a verification admission's lock — to the child, so ownership\n    outlives this process for exactly as long as the child and its own children run.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        if timeout is None and deadline is None:\n            return subprocess.run(\n                command,\n                cwd=root,\n                env=env,\n                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                capture_output=True,\n                text=True,\n                errors=\"replace\",\n                check=False,\n                pass_fds=pass_fds,\n            )\n        process = None\n        try:\n            with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                    raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted; no program starts\")\n                with defer_launch_signals():\n                    # Admission and waiting for the launch lock use the same round budget.\n                    # Recheck at process creation so a late replacement is never consumed.\n                    if deadline is not None:\n                        left = remaining(deadline)\n                        timeout = left if timeout is None else min(timeout, left)\n                    process = subprocess.Popen(\n                        command,\n                        cwd=root,\n                        env=env,\n                        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        text=True,\n                        errors=\"replace\",\n                        start_new_session=True,\n                        pass_fds=pass_fds,\n                    )\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.add(process.pid)\n            # Cancellation may have arrived while Popen was starting in a worker.\n            if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted during launch\")\n            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)\n            # A grandchild that kept running after the command exited would outlive an admission\n            # released around this call; the group is ended before returning (review row F6-5).\n            verify_lock.end_lingering_group(process.pid)\n        except BaseException:\n            if process is None:\n                raise\n            # Kill before unregistering and before any Popen cleanup could wait for a live child.\n            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)\n            with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):\n                process.communicate(timeout=KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS)\n            raise\n        finally:\n            if process is not None:\n                for pipe in (process.stdout, process.stderr):\n                    if pipe is not None:\n                        pipe.close()\n                with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.discard(process.pid)\n        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:\n        what = limit or f\"the reviewer time limit after {REVIEWER_MINUTES:",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0007-stage-2-reviews-by-codex-and-glm.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 133,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it. Until that is built, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3 runs the two phases:\n   Haiku 4.5 explores and Sonnet 5.5 implements. This is an open item of the\n   change, not a claim that it works.\n6. **Endpoints are architecture; the models on them are declaration\n   (amended on 2026-10-30).** Which endpoints framework content may reach\n   stays this ADR's matter (decision 2) and its amendments'. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture. A newly admitted\n   model takes a place in the review loop's ladder only; any other role\n   (explore, implem",

          "excerpt": "DENIED_TOOLS: dict[str, str] = {\n    \"sys_os_write\": \"writes a file\",\n    \"sys_os_edit\": \"edits a file\",\n    \"sys_os_shell\": \"runs a shell command, unconfined without a sandbox\",\n    \"sys_agent_download\": \"writes an agent archive into the working directory\",\n    \"sys_terminal_launch\": \"starts a shell in a terminal\",\n    \"sys_terminal_send\": \"types into a terminal\",\n    \"sys_terminal_close\": \"kills a terminal\",\n    \"sys_session_create\": \"starts a child session\",\n    \"sys_session_send\": \"messages a child session\",\n    \"sys_session_message\": \"sends work to another session of the same user\",\n    \"sys_session_close\": \"archives a session and stops its processes\",\n    \"sys_session_rename\": \"retitles a session\",\n    \"sys_session_share\": \"exposes a session's transcript\",\n    \"sys_scheduled_task_create\": \"creates a scheduled job\",\n    \"sys_scheduled_task_update\": \"changes a scheduled job\",\n    \"sys_scheduled_task_delete\": \"deletes a scheduled job\",\n    \"sys_call_async\": \"runs any granted tool in the background, sys_os_shell included\",\n    \"sys_cancel_async\": \"cancels a background call\",\n    \"sys_cancel_task\": \"cancels a task or a child session\",\n    \"sys_read_inbox\": \"empties the inbox and writes a receipt\",\n    \"sys_add_policy\": \"adds a policy to the session\",\n    \"ui_open_file\": \"opens a file in the user's open Omnigent windows\",\n    \"update_comment\": \"changes a review comment's status\",\n    \"browser_navigate\": \"loads a URL in a live page\",\n    \"browser_click\": \"acts on a live page\",\n    \"browser_type\": \"types into a live page\",\n    \"hindsight_retain\": \"sends session content to an outside memory service\",\n    \"hindsight_recall\": \"sends session content to an outside memory service\",\n    \"hindsight_reflect\": \"sends session content to an outside memory service\",\n}\n",

          "citation": "scripts/machine_facts.py::jobs_field",
          "end_line": 256,
          "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        elif not table:\n            raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        for line in table:\n            parts = line.split(None, 2)\n            if (\n                len(parts) != 3\n                or not parts[0].isdigit()\n                or not run_report.ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1])\n                or not parts[2].strip()\n            ):\n                raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        rows = run_report.parse_processes(raw, changes)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        lines.append(str(error))\n        return lines\n    if not rows:\n        if run_report.stage2 is not None:\n            lines.append(\"none matched\")\n        return lines\n    lines.extend(f\"pid {row.pid} · {row.label} · change {row.change} · elapsed {row.elapsed}\" for row in rows)\n    return lines\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "end_line": 388,
          "excerpt": "def _stage2_row(tokens: list[str], pid: str, elapsed: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> ProcessRow | None:\n    script = next((i for i, token in enumerate(tokens) if _is_stage2_script(token)), None)\n    if script is None or script + 1 >= len(tokens) or tokens[script + 1] not in KNOWN_VERBS:\n        return None\n    if script != 0:\n        if not re.fullmatch(r\"python(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*)?\", Path(tokens[0]).name):\n            return None  # the executable owns the invocation, not a preceding argument\n        if any(not token.startswith(\"-\") or token in {\"-c\", \"-m\", \"--\"} for token in tokens[1:script]):\n            return None\n    verb = tokens[script + 1]\n    change = NOT_READ\n    arguments = iter(tokens[script + 2 :])\n    value_options = {\n        \"--model\",\n        \"--class\",\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        \"--seats\",\n        \"--handover\",\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        \"--reason\",\n        \"--root\",\n    }\n    for token in arguments:\n        if token == \"--stage2-off\":\n            # Its reason is optional. A known change or another option must\n            # remain available to the positional/option reader below.\n            following = next(arguments, None)\n            if following is None:\n                break\n            if following not in changes and not following.startswith(\"-\"):\n                continue  # the explicit reason\n            token = following\n        if token in value_options:\n            next(arguments, None)\n            continue\n        if token.startswith(\"-\"):\n            continue  # options may stand between the verb and the change\n        if token in changes:\n            change = token\n        break  # only the first non-option token can name the change\n    return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=verb,",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_timeout_kills_the_whole_process_group(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"O188-4: a grandchild of the stopped step does not survive.\"\"\"\n    # Planted fault: a timed-out group's descendant survives, or the post-kill drain is unbounded.\n    pidfile = tmp_path / \"grandchild.pid\"\n    handed: list[float | None] = []  # every timeout a communicate was given, the drain's included\n    known: list[int] = []  # the grandchild's PID once complete, so cleanup can always reach it\n    real_popen = subprocess.Popen\n\n    def popen(command, *args, **kwargs):\n        process = real_popen(command, *args, **kwargs)\n        real_communicate = process.communicate\n\n        def communicate(timeout=None):\n            handed.append(timeout)\n            if len(handed) == 1:\n                # Readiness, not a race: the grandchild's complete PID is held before the expiry is injected.\n                pid = _await_complete_pid(pidfile, 200)\n                assert pid is not None, \"the timed step never wrote its grandchild's complete pid\"\n                known.append(pid)\n                raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(command, timeout)\n            return real_communicate(timeout=timeout)  # the bounded drain on the really killed group\n\n        process.communicate = communicate  # type: ignore[method-assign]\n        return process\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, \"Popen\", popen)\n    # The record is written to a temporary file and renamed into place: the name appears only complete.\n    staged = f\"{pidfile}.tmp\"\n    try:\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.CallFailed, match=\"stopped by\"):\n            stage2.launch(\n                [\"bash\", \"-c\", f\"sleep 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > {staged} && mv {staged} {pidfile}; wait\"],\n                tmp_path,\n                {**os.environ},\n                timeout=1,\n                limit=\"the test limit\",\n            )\n        assert handed[0] == 1, \"the step was handed more than its allowance\"\n        assert handed[1] == stage2.KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS, \"the kill's drain is unbounded\"\n        (pid,) = known\n        for _ in range(100):  # watchdog only: the kill is delivered at once, the exit is reaped a moment later\n            if not _child_alive(pid):\n                return\n            time.sleep(0.02)\n        pytest.fail(\"the grandchild of the timed-out step is still running\")\n    finally:\n        # cleanup: every known PID is killed; a missing or already dead one is tolerated\n        _kill_known(known[0] if known else _complete_pid(pidfile))\n",

          "excerpt": "# Spec — stage2-session\n\nStart a declared interactive Pi (for OpenCode Go models) or Codex session from\none checked runner invocation, in the change's worktree, with an auditable\nhandover. Since 2026-10-09 the OpenCode Go path launches Pi, not\nthe OpenCode CLI (maintainer, German: \"ich will keine opencode mehr\nbenutzen\"; answers Q-1 to Q-6 in `decisions.md`). The OpenCode Go service and\nits endpoint declaration are unchanged.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe runner has no interactive launch verb on main at `1c79860`. Direct TUI\nlaunches skip its declaration, prompt scan and audit. Budget takeover must\nnot open a second unchecked entry point. The Flash runner (`11abf42`,\nPR #89), which changes the same file, is on main (read 2026-10-09). Pi asks for no approval and has no sandbox\n(`docs/security.md` of the pinned Pi 1.1.0), so the repository must supply\nthe session policy itself, as an extension loaded explicitly by the runner\n(`research.md`, addendum of 2026-10-09).\n\n## Terms\n\n- **Dispatch:** Terminal accepted the launch command; not evidence that the\n  CLI started, model authenticated, answered, finished the workflow or passed\n  verification. Executables must exist at preflight; later startup failures\n  appear in the new window.\n- **Launch snapshot:** the state scanned before dispatch, not later edits,\n  later prompts or later UI model switches.\n\n## Supported models and prerequisites\n\nThe currently usable positive path is `--model gpt-6.1-sol`, through the\ndeclared `openai-codex` endpoint and official Codex CLI. The Pi path accepts\n`opencode-go/<model>` only when the `opencode-go` endpoint lists that model\nfor framework content in `model-endpoints.yaml` (declared by ADR 0011; the\nid names the endpoint, not the launcher, Q-5). The runner does not invent a\nreview ordering and starts only the Pi pinned by `require_pi` (1.1.0); any\nother Pi is refused before dispatch. Fixture-only positive tests supply an\nexplicitly declared endpoint, not a production allow-list.\n\nThe dedicated worktree of change `<change>` is the canonical path\n`<main checkout>/.claude/worktrees/<change>`, where the main checkout is the\nparent of git's shared `.git` directory. A change folder copied into another\nworktree does not confer ownership; only this path with an attached branch\nqualifies. The invocation's working directory and runner root must both be\nthat canonical worktree root, not a subdirectory, another worktree or main.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When `python3 scripts/stage2.py session <change> --model <id>` runs in the\n   change's dedicated worktree, it accepts the declared supported model.\n   *Refuted by:* no session parser, or dispatch from the main checkout,\n   detached HEAD or a different root than the validated change.\n2. If the endpoint/model declaration is absent, ambiguous, unreadable or\n   disallows framework content, the command refuses before terminal dispatch.\n   *Refuted by:* an unknown model, unapproved transport, missing residency\n   or malformed declaration reaching the terminal stand-in.\n3. When the handover is supplied, its actual text becomes the first prompt;\n   otherwise the change-local `handover.md` is used.\n   *Refuted by:* an empty/missing/unreadable/nonregular file being accepted,\n   only a pathname being sent, or an unrelated handover silently selected.\n   Prompts over 32 KiB UTF-8 or containing NUL refuse before dispatch; the\n   complete dispatch command is bounded to 64 KiB to fit the launch transport.\n4. If a handover path resolves outside the validated worktree, it is refused.\n   *Refuted by:* traversal or a symlink sending outside-file text to a model.\n5.           "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **The job** — the recurring re-check of one research note.\n- **The note** — the one file under `docs/research/` a run re-checks.\n- **The list** — the output of `python3 scripts/check_research_currency.py\n  --format json` (pull request #73, schema version 1); `notes[0]` is its\n  first entry.\n- **The run date** — the calendar date, in the maintainer's time zone, on\n  which a run starts, written `YYYY-MM-DD`.\n- **The base** — the commit of `origin/main` a run starts from.\n- **The addendum** — the one section a run appends at the end of the note:\n  the heading `## Addendum <run date> · re-check`, then the four\n  subsections `### Holds`, `### Overtaken`, `### New`, `### Not read`, in\n  this order.           "excerpt": "### Night runs\n\nA night run works its queue alone and sequentially; two standing rules\n(maintainer, 2026-10-26; bead coding-harness-yuw.4) keep it moving where a\nday session would ask:\n\n1. **Codex at capacity:** wait four minutes and retry once. If the retry\n   fails too, Sonnet 5.5 takes that one step — a repair through\n   `stage2.py repair <change> --stage2-off \"<reason>\"`, a phase-6 review or\n   re-check through a read-only Sonnet 5.5 sub-agent whose rows the\n   orchestrator records unchanged. The step carries a note with the reason,\n   and the run continues. The runner automates this once bead\n   coding-harness-m98e lands.\n2. **A further case of the same mechanism at a phase-6 re-check:** record\n   the finding, park that pull request and continue with the next queue\n   item; the maintainer decides it in the morning.\n\n**The night profile (since the night-stall-guard change, 2026-11-09; bead\ncoding-harness-ibde).** An unattended session starts Claude Code through the\nnight launcher so a permission question cannot hold the run:\n`python3 ~/.claude/night.py` followed by the arguments a normal `claude` call\nwould take. The launcher reads the explicit ask and deny rules of the supported\nsettings scopes, turns every sourced ask rule into a deny in a private overlay,\nand runs `claude --settings <overlay> --permission-mode dontAsk` for this\ninvocation only; the day settings are never rewritten, and the overlay lives in\na temporary directory for the child's lifetime. A denied action therefore\nreturns control at once instead of waiting for a person: the session continues\nwith an authorised alternative, or parks the denied step and records it — it\nnever disables the brake to get through. The launch is refused before `claude`\nstarts when a present settings file cannot be read or parsed, or when a caller\nargument would replace the profile (`--settings`, `--permission-mode`,\n`--dangerously-skip-permissions`). What the profile does not cover stays as it\nis: external policy and authentication dialogs, a stopped or usage-limited\nsession, and — until the maintainer chooses a push service — no phone alert\nand no independent heartbeat exists.\n\n**The 30-minute wake (standing since 2026-11-05/06; bead\ncoding-harness-7x3c).** Supervision of an unattended run rests on scheduled\nreturns of control, not on session-only timers that die with their session\nand not on idle polling. A **wake** is a scheduled return of control to the\norchestrating session; elapsed time or a printed message alone does not\nestablish delivery. A **lane** is one worktree with the change it serves;\nthe run's active lanes — those with authorised work still eligible to run —\nform the watch list. Before a run enters unattended operation, its session\ncreates a run-specific state directory under\n`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/night/<run-id>/` holding\n`lanes.txt`, a `busy/` directory and an append-only `lane-watch.log`, so a\nsuccessor session can resume the run from the files without chat memory.\nChoose `<run-id>` as the UTC start date plus an unused letter, for example\n`2026-11-06-a`; concurrent runs on that date take different letters. Record\nthe run id and state-directory path in the run's handover file under\n`docs/journal/handover/<date>-<name>.md`. This is the record for parked\nquestions, completed-lane outcomes and the end reason throughout this\nroutine, not a change's `handover.md` or the session-notes safety net.\nA successor finds the run id in that handover and reuses its directory,\nnever creating a second directory for the resumed run. The state directory\nrecords the run's wake and keep-awake handles and busy-marker ownership;\na successor taking over that run uses this record to manage its resources,\nincluding handles started by the preceding session. A lane entry names the\nlane id, its worktree, the current item and the next authorised action, and is updated whenever the work changes.           "excerpt": "## Non-goals\n\n- A new scheduler, daemon, model call, notification service or automatic\n  restart of an unavailable session; delivery uses the harness's existing\n  scheduling or background-completion facility.\n- The broader lane diary/planner, status-line integration and automatic\n  backlog selection proposed for lane planning and lane watch (beads\n  coding-harness-4emv and coding-harness-5q2p).\n- Runner process supervision, recap-lock repair, tracker lease renewal,\n  new concurrency limits or new permission to merge or start work.\n- Promoting the trial watchdog's 120-second polling and ten-minute idle\n  threshold to standing requirements; the accepted periodic wake is 30 minutes.\n- A universal promise to dispatch immediately between wakes: “at once” means\n  at the check that detects idle work, also including ordinary job completion.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-heartbeat/spec.md",
          "reference": "Non-goals",
          "start_line": 96,
          "supported": true,

          "excerpt": "## Non-goals\n\n- The phone alert, permission-prompt monitoring and missing-heartbeat alert:\n  return after these safeguards, when the maintainer chooses the push service.\n- A scheduler, daemon, headless heartbeat architecture, automatic restart,\n  lane planner, runner process watchdog, dashboard or notification service.\n- Changing merge authority, approving a merge, bypassing another permission\n  system, or changing permissions of Codex, Pi or Omnigent itself.\n- Implementing the response to a denied call in `scripts/stage2.py`.\n- Phase 2b and an ADR: this bounded change configures the existing permission\n  boundary without changing the architecture, as the answered interview states.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "citation": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-stall-guard/decisions.md::Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall",
          "end_line": 43,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall\n\nasked: 2026-11-09\nanswer: \"Ja\" — the change ships, in this order: (1) a night settings profile in which every rule that would ask the maintainer denies instead, so a call returns at once and the orchestrator takes another path; (2) a precise merge brake that asks (by day) or denies (at night) only for real merges — `gh pr merge`, the REST merge endpoint and the GraphQL mutations that merge or enqueue — while a read query that only names merge fields passes; (3) the phone alert for an open permission prompt and for a missing heartbeat comes after (1) and (2), as the second safeguard. The push service for (3) is not chosen yet and is asked when (3) is built.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: on 2026-11-08 at 22:26 UTC a read-only `gh api graphql` status query that named the fields mergedAt and isInMergeQueue matched the ask rule `Bash(gh api *merge*)` in .claude/settings.json; the orchestrating session waited for approval until 06:04 UTC and every heartbeat, watchdog wake-up and task notification queued behind it (session transcript), so finished lanes idled about 5.5 hours.\n  Intention: no single question may hold the night; the maintainer asked first how to stop the blocking at all (\"Wie kann ich es erstmal verhindern dass überhaupt alle Prozesse blockiert werden\").\n  Today: ask rules wait without limit; nothing alerts the maintainer; the watchdog only wakes the chat, which cannot act while a prompt is open.\n  Repository change: a night profile under tools/claude-code/ (installed by tools/claude-code/install.sh), narrowed merge rules in .claude/settings.json with tests of the rule set; the alert later.\n  Architecture change: none; moving each heartbeat into its own headless, time-limited call (launchd) belongs to the harness-neutral night-run work, not to this change.\n\nIn the context of the night run, whose orchestration lives in one chat that a\nsingle open permission prompt can hold for hours, facing ask rules that wait\nwithout limit and a merge brake that matched a read-only status query, we\ndecided to deny instead of ask at night and to narrow the merge brake to real\nmerges first, and to add a phone alert afterwards, to achieve that no question\ncan stop the night again, accepting that a denied call at night fails at once\nand the orchestrator must take another path — 2026-11-09\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-stall-guard/decisions.md",
          "reference": "Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall",

          "truncated": false
        },

          "excerpt": "## Addendum — 2026-11-05, ending the session with jobs running\n\nThe six runner jobs are children of this Claude Code session; ending the\nsession most likely stops them mid-attempt (not measured). If a worktree then\nshows uncommitted changes and its findings.md has no closing line for the last\nattempt, discard the partial attempt (`git checkout -- . && git clean -fd`\ninside that worktree only, after reading `git status`) and start the same\nverb again; every earlier step is committed and pushed.\n",

          "end_line": 43,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall\n\nasked: 2026-11-09\nanswer: \"Ja\" — the change ships, in this order: (1) a night settings profile in which every rule that would ask the maintainer denies instead, so a call returns at once and the orchestrator takes another path; (2) a precise merge brake that asks (by day) or denies (at night) only for real merges — `gh pr merge`, the REST merge endpoint and the GraphQL mutations that merge or enqueue — while a read query that only names merge fields passes; (3) the phone alert for an open permission prompt and for a missing heartbeat comes after (1) and (2), as the second safeguard. The push service for (3) is not chosen yet and is asked when (3) is built.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: on 2026-11-08 at 22:26 UTC a read-only `gh api graphql` status query that named the fields mergedAt and isInMergeQueue matched the ask rule `Bash(gh api *merge*)` in .claude/settings.json; the orchestrating session waited for approval until 06:04 UTC and every heartbeat, watchdog wake-up and task notification queued behind it (session transcript), so finished lanes idled about 5.5 hours.\n  Intention: no single question may hold the night; the maintainer asked first how to stop the blocking at all (\"Wie kann ich es erstmal verhindern dass überhaupt alle Prozesse blockiert werden\").\n  Today: ask rules wait without limit; nothing alerts the maintainer; the watchdog only wakes the chat, which cannot act while a prompt is open.\n  Repository change: a night profile under tools/claude-code/ (installed by tools/claude-code/install.sh), narrowed merge rules in .claude/settings.json with tests of the rule set; the alert later.\n  Architecture change: none; moving each heartbeat into its own headless, time-limited call (launchd) belongs to the harness-neutral night-run work, not to this change.\n\nIn the context of the night run, whose orchestration lives in one chat that a\nsingle open permission prompt can hold for hours, facing ask rules that wait\nwithout limit and a merge brake that matched a read-only status query, we\ndecided to deny instead of ask at night and to narrow the merge brake to real\nmerges first, and to add a phone alert afterwards, to achieve that no question\ncan stop the night again, accepting that a denied call at night fails at once\nand the orchestrator must take another path — 2026-11-09\n",

          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair.           "citation": "AGENTS.md::Sessions across checkouts",
          "end_line": 190,
          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair. Reason: a run's history cannot be reset, and asking each time stopped\n  lanes overnight.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_timeout_kills_the_whole_process_group(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"O188-4: a grandchild of the stopped step does not survive.\"\"\"\n    # Planted fault: a timed-out group's descendant survives, or the post-kill drain is unbounded.\n    pidfile = tmp_path / \"grandchild.pid\"\n    handed: list[float | None] = []  # every timeout a communicate was given, the drain's included\n    known: list[int] = []  # the grandchild's PID once complete, so cleanup can always reach it\n    real_popen = subprocess.Popen\n\n    def popen(command, *args, **kwargs):\n        process = real_popen(command, *args, **kwargs)\n        real_communicate = process.communicate\n\n        def communicate(timeout=None):\n            handed.append(timeout)\n            if len(handed) == 1:\n                # Readiness, not a race: the grandchild's complete PID is held before the expiry is injected.\n                pid = _await_complete_pid(pidfile, 200)\n                assert pid is not None, \"the timed step never wrote its grandchild's complete pid\"\n                known.append(pid)\n                raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(command, timeout)\n            return real_communicate(timeout=timeout)  # the bounded drain on the really killed group\n\n        process.communicate = communicate  # type: ignore[method-assign]\n        return process\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, \"Popen\", popen)\n    # The record is written to a temporary file and renamed into place: the name appears only complete.\n    staged = f\"{pidfile}.tmp\"\n    try:\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.CallFailed, match=\"stopped by\"):\n            stage2.launch(\n                [\"bash\", \"-c\", f\"sleep 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > {staged} && mv {staged} {pidfile}; wait\"],\n                tmp_path,\n                {**os.environ},\n                timeout=1,\n                limit=\"the test limit\",\n            )\n        assert handed[0] == 1, \"the step was handed more than its allowance\"\n        assert handed[1] == stage2.KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS, \"the kill's drain is unbounded\"\n        (pid,) = known\n        for _ in range(100):  # watchdog only: the kill is delivered at once, the exit is reaped a moment later\n            if not _child_alive(pid):\n                return\n            time.sleep(0.02)\n        pytest.fail(\"the grandchild of the timed-out step is still running\")\n    finally:\n        # cleanup: every known PID is killed; a missing or already dead one is tolerated\n        _kill_known(known[0] if known else _complete_pid(pidfile))\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_reap_does_not_hang_without_new_session_and_ignored_sigterm():\n    m = module()\n    script = (\n        \"import signal,time\\nsignal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)\\n\"\n        \"print('partial',flush=True)\\ntime.sleep(60)\\n\"\n    )\n    procs = {}\n\n    def launcher(slot, _allowance):\n        proc = subprocess.Popen(\n            [sys.executable, \"-c\", slot.payload], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True\n        )\n        procs[slot.slot_id] = proc\n        return proc\n\n    t0 = time.monotonic()\n    result = m.dispatch(\n        [make_slot(\"a\", script=script, allowance=0.5)],\n        gate=Harness().gate,\n        launcher=launcher,\n        grace=0.5,\n    )\n    assert time.monotonic() - t0 < 10\n    assert by_id(result)[\"a\"].outcome == \"timed-out\"\n    assert procs[\"a\"].poll() is not None\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_cancellation_kills_group_after_leader_was_already_reaped():\n    \"\"\"F-44: cancellation still owns a surviving group after its leader was reaped.\"\"\"\n    m = module()\n    script = (\n        \"import os,signal,time\\n\"\n        \"if os.fork() == 0:\\n\"\n        \"    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)\\n\"\n        \"    print(os.getpid(), flush=True)\\n\"\n        \"    time.sleep(60)\\n\"\n        \"else:\\n\"\n        \"    os._exit(0)\\n\"\n    )\n    proc = subprocess.Popen(\n        [sys.executable, \"-c\", script],\n        start_new_session=True,\n        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n        text=True,\n    )\n    descendant = int(proc.stdout.readline())\n    proc.wait(timeout=5)  # the process group leader is gone before cancellation starts\n    try:\n        out, err = m._stop_and_reap(proc, 0.1)\n        assert (out, err) == (\"\", \"\")\n        alive = True\n        for _ in range(100):\n            try:\n                os.kill(descendant, 0)\n            except ProcessLookupError:\n                alive = False\n                break\n            time.sleep(0.05)\n        assert not alive, \"the reaped leader's descendant survived cancellation\"\n    finally:\n        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):\n            os.kill(descendant, signal.SIGKILL)\n",

          "excerpt": "def kill_live() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Kill the process group of every timed program still running; return how many were signalled.\"\"\"\n    _LAUNCH_STOPPED.set()\n    with _LIVE_LOCK:\n        groups = sorted(_LIVE_GROUPS)\n    for group in groups:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            os.killpg(group, signal.SIGKILL)\n    return len(groups)\n",

        {
          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::launch",
          "end_line": 1150,
          "excerpt": "def launch(\n    command: list[str],\n    root: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str],\n    secret: str | list[str] | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    pass_fds: tuple[int, ...] = (),\n) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    \"\"\"Start a foreign program: empty standard input, the worktree as its directory.\n\n    With a `timeout` the program leads a process group of its own, and a timeout kills the whole\n    group: a hung `make verify` leaves no shell, pytest or worker behind to write into the worktree\n    after the run stopped (O188-4 of the #188 review). The group is registered while it runs, so an\n    interrupted runner kills it too (`kill_live`), and the drain after a kill is bounded by\n    `KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS`: a descendant that left the group is abandoned, not waited for.\n    `pass_fds` hands descriptors — a verification admission's lock — to the child, so ownership\n    outlives this process for exactly as long as the child and its own children run.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        if timeout is None and deadline is None:\n            return subprocess.run(\n                command,\n                cwd=root,\n                env=env,\n                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                capture_output=True,\n                text=True,\n                errors=\"replace\",\n                check=False,\n                pass_fds=pass_fds,\n            )\n        process = None\n        try:\n            with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                    raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted; no program starts\")\n                with defer_launch_signals():\n                    # Admission and waiting for the launch lock use the same round budget.\n                    # Recheck at process creation so a late replacement is never consumed.\n                    if deadline is not None:\n                        left = remaining(deadline)\n                        timeout = left if timeout is None else min(timeout, left)\n                    process = subprocess.Popen(\n                        command,\n                        cwd=root,\n                        env=env,\n                        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        text=True,\n                        errors=\"replace\",\n                        start_new_session=True,\n                        pass_fds=pass_fds,\n                    )\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.add(process.pid)\n            # Cancellation may have arrived while Popen was starting in a worker.\n            if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted during launch\")\n            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)\n            # A grandchild that kept running after the command exited would outlive an admission\n            # released around this call; the group is ended before returning (review row F6-5).\n            verify_lock.end_lingering_group(process.pid)\n        except BaseException:\n            if process is None:\n                raise\n            # Kill before unregistering and before any Popen cleanup could wait for a live child.\n            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)\n            with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):\n                process.communicate(timeout=KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS)\n            raise\n        finally:\n            if process is not None:\n                for pipe in (process.stdout, process.stderr):\n                    if pip",

A process that already holds\n    or is acquiring an independent admission is refused before any queueing.\n    Refusals raise VerifyLockRefused or MemoryFloorRefused before the body\n    runs; release happens in every ending, after any child cleanup the caller\n    does.\n    \"\"\"\n    inherited = nested_holder_pid()\n    if inherited is not None:\n        _log(f\"inheriting admission from pid {inherited}; no queue and no memory wait\")\n        yield None\n        return\n    with _independent_admission_guard():\n        setting = verify_slots_setting()\n        admission = _Admission(_prepare_state(), command, setting)\n        try:\n            admission.enter()\n        except BaseException:\n            admission.release()\n            raise\n        try:\n            yield admission.pass_fds()\n        finally:\n            admission.release()\n",

          "excerpt": "def inherit_env(env: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The environment a local check runs under, with the admission state it must carry.\n\n    This is additive and local-only: a runner's allowlist stays closed, foreign\n    calls receive none of these names, and a genuine inherited marker travels\n    so a nested check reuses its ancestor's admission even after local\n    environment filtering.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = dict(env)\n    env[\"XDG_STATE_HOME\"] = str(state_base())\n    if FLOOR_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[FLOOR_ENV] = os.environ[FLOOR_ENV]\n    # The slot setting travels to local children when present, so a nested\n    # runner's own protected work — never a nested entry, which parses\n    # nothing — sees the same configuration its parent had (criterion 2).\n    # The foreign-model environment allowlist stays closed to HARNESS_*.\n    if SLOTS_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[SLOTS_ENV] = os.environ[SLOTS_ENV]\n    nested = nested_holder_pid()\n    marker, token = (nested, os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV)) if nested is not None else (_active_pid(), _active_token())\n    if marker is not None and token:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(marker)\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = token\n    else:\n        env.pop(LOCK_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(TOKEN_ENV, None)\n    # The admission context resolves the same way the child itself would: its\n    # own active admission, an inherited one, or nothing (bead\n    # coding-harness-1um6).           "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        elif not table:\n            raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        for line in table:\n            parts = line.split(None, 2)\n            if (\n                len(parts) != 3\n                or not parts[0].isdigit()\n                or not run_report.ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1])\n                or not parts[2].strip()\n            ):\n                raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        rows = run_report.parse_processes(raw, changes)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        lines.append(str(error))\n        return lines\n    if not rows:\n        if run_report.stage2 is not None:\n            lines.append(\"none matched\")\n        return lines\n    lines.extend(f\"pid {row.pid} · {row.label} · change {row.change} · elapsed {row.elapsed}\" for row in rows)\n    return lines\n",

          "excerpt": "def _stage2_row(tokens: list[str], pid: str, elapsed: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> ProcessRow | None:\n    script = next((i for i, token in enumerate(tokens) if _is_stage2_script(token)), None)\n    if script is None or script + 1 >= len(tokens) or tokens[script + 1] not in KNOWN_VERBS:\n        return None\n    if script != 0:\n        if not re.fullmatch(r\"python(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*)?\", Path(tokens[0]).name):\n            return None  # the executable owns the invocation, not a preceding argument\n        if any(not token.startswith(\"-\") or token in {\"-c\", \"-m\", \"--\"} for token in tokens[1:script]):\n            return None\n    verb = tokens[script + 1]\n    change = NOT_READ\n    arguments = iter(tokens[script + 2 :])\n    value_options = {\n        \"--model\",\n        \"--class\",\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        \"--seats\",\n        \"--handover\",\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        \"--reason\",\n        \"--root\",\n    }\n    for token in arguments:\n        if token == \"--stage2-off\":\n            # Its reason is optional. A known change or another option must\n            # remain available to the positional/option reader below.\n            following = next(arguments, None)\n            if following is None:\n                break\n            if following not in changes and not following.startswith(\"-\"):\n                continue  # the explicit reason\n            token = following\n        if token in value_options:\n            next(arguments, None)\n            continue\n        if token.startswith(\"-\"):\n            continue  # options may stand between the verb and the change\n        if token in changes:\n            change = token\n        break  # only the first non-option token can name the change\n    return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=verb,",

Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06).           "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Night runs",
          "end_line": 2325,
          "excerpt": "### Night runs\n\nA night run works its queue alone and sequentially; two standing rules\n(maintainer, 2026-10-26; bead coding-harness-yuw.4) keep it moving where a\nday session would ask:\n\n1. **Codex at capacity:** wait four minutes and retry once. If the retry\n   fails too, Sonnet 5.5 takes that one step — a repair through\n   `stage2.py repair <change> --stage2-off \"<reason>\"`, a phase-6 review or\n   re-check through a read-only Sonnet 5.5 sub-agent whose rows the\n   orchestrator records unchanged. The step carries a note with the reason,\n   and the run continues. The runner automates this once bead\n   coding-harness-m98e lands.\n2. **A further case of the same mechanism at a phase-6 re-check:** record\n   the finding, park that pull request and continue with the next queue\n   item; the maintainer decides it in the morning.\n\n**The night profile (since the night-stall-guard change, 2026-11-09; bead\ncoding-harness-ibde).** An unattended session starts Claude Code through the\nnight launcher so a permission question cannot hold the run:\n`python3 ~/.claude/night.py` followed by the arguments a normal `claude` call\nwould take. The launcher reads the explicit ask and deny rules of the supported\nsettings scopes, turns every sourced ask rule into a deny in a private overlay,\nand runs `claude --settings <overlay> --permission-mode dontAsk` for this\ninvocation only; the day settings are never rewritten, and the overlay lives in\na temporary directory for the child's lifetime. A denied action therefore\nreturns control at once instead of waiting for a person: the session continues\nwith an authorised alternative, or parks the denied step and records it — it\nnever disables the brake to get through. The launch is refused before `claude`\nstarts when a present settings file cannot be read or parsed, or when a caller\nargument would replace the profile (`--settings`, `--permission-mode`,\n`--dangerously-skip-permissions`). What the profile does not cover stays as it\nis: external policy and authentication dialogs, a stopped or usage-limited\nsession, and — until the maintainer chooses a push service — no phone alert\nand no independent heartbeat exists.\n\n**The 30-minute wake (standing since 2026-11-05/06; bead\ncoding-harness-7x3c).** Supervision of an unattended run rests on scheduled\nreturns of control, not on session-only timers that die with their session\nand not on idle polling. A **wake** is a scheduled return of control to the\norchestrating session; elapsed time or a printed message alone does not\nestablish delivery. A **lane** is one worktree with the change it serves;\nthe run's active lanes — those with authorised work still eligible to run —\nform the watch list. Record\nthe run id and state-directory path in the run's handover file under\n`docs/journal/handover/<date>-<name>.md`. This is the record for parked\nquestions, completed-lane outcomes and the end reason throughout this\nroutine, not a change's `handover.md` or the session-notes safety net.\nA successor finds the run id in that handover and reuses its directory,\nnever creating a second directory for the resumed run.       "statement": "A detached job that starts the next lane step without the orchestrating session collides with the night-run busy-marker discipline: an apparent leftover marker must be checked against its owner's current activity before anything is dispatched — never launch a duplicate on a marker's strength — and a resumed session must reuse the run's existing state directory rather than create a second one. The evidence this collision happens in practice is recorded: on 2026-11-23 01:10–07:05 every running job ended and no wake-up reached the session, and on 2026-11-05 six runner jobs were children of the ending session and likely stopped mid-attempt."

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1506,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuse",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::launch",
          "end_line": 1150,
          "excerpt": "def launch(\n    command: list[str],\n    root: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str],\n    secret: str | list[str] | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    pass_fds: tuple[int, ...] = (),\n) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    \"\"\"Start a foreign program: empty standard input, the worktree as its directory.\n\n    With a `timeout` the program leads a process group of its own, and a timeout kills the whole\n    group: a hung `make verify` leaves no shell, pytest or worker behind to write into the worktree\n    after the run stopped (O188-4 of the #188 review). The group is registered while it runs, so an\n    interrupted runner kills it too (`kill_live`), and the drain after a kill is bounded by\n    `KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS`: a descendant that left the group is abandoned, not waited for.\n    `pass_fds` hands descriptors — a verification admission's lock — to the child, so ownership\n    outlives this process for exactly as long as the child and its own children run.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        if timeout is None and deadline is None:\n            return subprocess.run(\n                command,\n                cwd=root,\n                env=env,\n                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                capture_output=True,\n                text=True,\n                errors=\"replace\",\n                check=False,\n                pass_fds=pass_fds,\n            )\n        process = None\n        try:\n            with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                    raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted; no program starts\")\n                with defer_launch_signals():\n                    # Admission and waiting for the launch lock use the same round budget.\n                    # Recheck at process creation so a late replacement is never consumed.\n                    if deadline is not None:\n                        left = remaining(deadline)\n                        timeout = left if timeout is None else min(timeout, left)\n                    process = subprocess.Popen(\n                        command,\n                        cwd=root,\n                        env=env,\n                        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        text=True,\n                        errors=\"replace\",\n                        start_new_session=True,\n                        pass_fds=pass_fds,\n                    )\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.add(process.pid)\n            # Cancellation may have arrived while Popen was starting in a worker.\n            if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted during launch\")\n            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)\n            # A grandchild that kept running after the command exited would outlive an admission\n            # released around this call; the group is ended before returning (review row F6-5).\n            verify_lock.end_lingering_group(process.pid)\n        except BaseException:\n            if process is None:\n                raise\n            # Kill before unregistering and before any Popen cleanup could wait for a live child.\n            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)\n            with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):\n                process.communicate(timeout=KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS)\n            raise\n        finally:\n            if process is not None:\n                for pipe in (process.stdout, process.stderr):\n                    if pipe is not None:\n                        pipe.close()\n                with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.discard(process.pid)\n        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:\n        what = limit or f\"the reviewer time limit a",

      "statement": "Per-call and teardown bounds a detached long job inherits today: the runner's timed launch kills the whole group on timeout, a descendant that left the group is abandoned after KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS (5 s), a signal during process creation leaves no child, and an interrupted runner kills its running programs — each pinned by tests. A detached job deliberately escapes these bounds, so the pins describe the boundary the change moves: who kills the detached child's grandchildren, and who reaps a detached child whose launcher already exited (the research dispatcher's _stop_and_reap/_own_group and verify_lock's _watch_child are the existing reap patterns)."
    }
