          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair. Reason: a run's history cannot be reset, and asking each time stopped\n  lanes overnight.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021).           "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`). By\n   hand: `git fetch origin && git worktree add -b <branch>\n   .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main`. `bd worktree create` works as well but\n   writes the worktree's path into the tracked `.gitignore`, which is one more\n   change in the diff. Sibling directories beside the repository are retired\n   (D-5); worktrees that still sit there are finished and removed, not moved.\n3. **Always from a freshly fetched `origin/main`.** A worktree on a stale base\n   produces a pull request that is behind before it opens.\n4. **The tracker needs nothing.** `tools/bd` in a worktree finds the main\n   checkout's tracker through the shared git directory — no variable, no\n   redirect file, no copy. Concurrent writers lose nothing and a contested\n   claim has exactly one winner (measured 2026-09-23 with bd 1.3.0). Who may\n   write is house rule 4: the first writing session writes the tracker; every\n   other session claims its one bead with `tools/bd update <id> --claim\n   --actor <session>` and leaves its handover comment on that bead, nothing\n   more. After tracker writes: `tools/bd dolt push` first, `git push` second.\n5. **Omnigent starts inside the worktree.** Omnigent runs Claude Code as its\n   authors intend (`omnigent claude --use-native-config`, ADR 0006); the session\n   is started from the worktree's directory, so its hooks, its\n   `.claude/settings.json` and `tools/bd` all resolve there. Omnigent's own\n   tools reach the session as `mcp__omnigent__<tool>`, and neither Claude\n   Code's path rules, the hooks on its file tools nor Omnigent's own Claude Code\n   hook see what they do. Each one that writes, runs, spawns or changes state is\n   therefore denied by name in `.claude/settings.json`; the read-only ones stay\n   usable, except one that may send the task text to a routing judge\n   (`sys_advise_models`), which the user is asked about each time\n   (`permissions.ask`; decision of 2026-09-29). The one list, with a reason per\n   tool, is `scripts/omnigent_policy.py`. Read-only tools stay usable.\n   The default policy in `tools/omnigent/` is the second layer, rendered from\n   that same list. It refuses the denied ones and asks about the asked one\n   server-side for every Omnigent session on the machine. The\n   maintainer installs it, and nothing here depends on it alone (ADR 0006); as of\n   2026-09-29 it is built but not installed. Omnigent's bridge runs its own\n   `sys_os_*` tools without any policy while its relay does not advertise them,\n   and there only the rule in `.claude/settings.json` holds. Not yet measured: whether `omnigent claude`\n   started inside a worktree keeps that directory as the session's working\n   directory in every case.\n6. **After the merge, the worktree goes.** `git worktree remove\n   .claude/worktrees/<name>` and the branch with it. A worktree nobody works in\n   is a place where a later session finds an old state and takes it for the\n   current one.\n\nIsolation between sessions is a working agreement, not a wall: worktrees share\ngit's refs, hooks and configuration (`docs/architecture/2026-09-17-gap-analysis.md`).\nWhat really does not happen is simultaneous writing *to the same change* — that\nis not a tool question but a division of work.\n\n**What i",

          "end_line": 1150,
          "excerpt": "def launch(\n    command: list[str],\n    root: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str],\n    secret: str | list[str] | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    pass_fds: tuple[int, ...] = (),\n) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    \"\"\"Start a foreign program: empty standard input, the worktree as its directory.\n\n    With a `timeout` the program leads a process group of its own, and a timeout kills the whole\n    group: a hung `make verify` leaves no shell, pytest or worker behind to write into the worktree\n    after the run stopped (O188-4 of the #188 review). The group is registered while it runs, so an\n    interrupted runner kills it too (`kill_live`), and the drain after a kill is bounded by\n    `KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS`: a descendant that left the group is abandoned, not waited for.\n    `pass_fds` hands descriptors — a verification admission's lock — to the child, so ownership\n    outlives this process for exactly as long as the child and its own children run.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        if timeout is None and deadline is None:\n            return subprocess.run(\n                command,\n                cwd=root,\n                env=env,\n                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                capture_output=True,\n                text=True,\n                errors=\"replace\",\n                check=False,\n                pass_fds=pass_fds,\n            )\n        process = None\n        try:\n            with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                    raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted; no program starts\")\n                with defer_launch_signals():\n                    # Admission and waiting for the launch lock use the same round budget.\n                    # Recheck at process creation so a late replacement is never consumed.\n                    if deadline is not None:\n                        left = remaining(deadline)\n                        timeout = left if timeout is None else min(timeout, left)\n                    process = subprocess.Popen(\n                        command,\n                        cwd=root,\n                        env=env,\n                        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        text=True,\n                        errors=\"replace\",\n                        start_new_session=True,\n                        pass_fds=pass_fds,\n                    )\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.add(process.pid)\n            # Cancellation may have arrived while Popen was starting in a worker.\n            if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted during launch\")\n            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)\n            # A grandchild that kept running after the command exited would outlive an admission\n            # released around this call; the group is ended before returning (review row F6-5).\n            verify_lock.end_lingering_group(process.pid)\n        except BaseException:\n            if process is None:\n                raise\n            # Kill before unregistering and before any Popen cleanup could wait for a live child.\n            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)\n            with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):\n                process.communicate(timeout=KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS)\n            raise\n        finally:\n            if process is not None:\n                for pipe in (process.stdout, process.stderr):\n                    if pipe is not None:\n                        pipe.close()\n                with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.discard(process.pid)\n        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:\n        what = limit or f\"the reviewer time limit after {REVIEWER_MINUTES:",

          "end_line": 256,
          "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        elif not table:\n            raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        for line in table:\n            parts = line.split(None, 2)\n            if (\n                len(parts) != 3\n                or not parts[0].isdigit()\n                or not run_report.ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1])\n                or not parts[2].strip()\n            ):\n                raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        rows = run_report.parse_processes(raw, changes)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        lines.append(str(error))\n        return lines\n    if not rows:\n        if run_report.stage2 is not None:\n            lines.append(\"none matched\")\n        return lines\n    lines.extend(f\"pid {row.pid} · {row.label} · change {row.change} · elapsed {row.elapsed}\" for row in rows)\n    return lines\n",

          "end_line": 464,
          "excerpt": "def parse_processes(ps_text: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> list[ProcessRow]:\n    \"\"\"The runner invocations and verification processes of one `ps` table.\n\n    Token matching only: a string inside an unrelated command - a shell\n    wrapper, an editor, an echo - is discarded, never reported.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for line in ps_text.splitlines():\n        parts = line.split(None, 2)\n        if len(parts) < 3 or not parts[0].isdigit() or not ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1]):\n            continue  # the header line and anything unshaped\n        pid, elapsed, command = parts\n        tokens = command.split()\n        if not tokens:\n            continue\n        row = _stage2_row(tokens, pid, elapsed, changes) or _verify_row(tokens, pid, elapsed)\n        if row is not None:\n            rows.append(row)\n    return rows\n",

      "author_utc": "2026-10-30T12:12:04Z",

      "author_utc": "2026-10-09T13:56:58Z",
      "body": "Work package 4 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi. An\nopencode-go/<model> id names the endpoint; it now starts the pinned Pi in the\nTerminal window, with discovery off and one policy extension loaded from a copy\nin the session's private directory, the declared model, and the prompt after\n`--`. The runner checks the pin with require_pi, confirms by `pi --help` in a\nscratch home that the extension's flag is listed, and refuses otherwise,\nremoving what it made. It hands over no key and sets no agent directory: Pi\nsigns in from the maintainer's own ~/.pi/agent (Q-6). A prompt that starts with\n@ is refused, because Pi would read it as a file name.\n\nThe seven OpenCode-only functions, AGENT and GUARDED are gone. The tests get a\npi stand-in beside codex and osascript, and an opencode stand-in that must\nnever be called; the 25 canned effective-policy answers are replaced by tests of\nthe version pin, the read-back, the @ prompt, the scratch home and the absence\nof a key. 19 planted faults in the runner all turn a test red.\n\nDocuments that describe the verb to a reader still say OpenCode until package 5.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",

    "30bf06b4f8c96d6465f61a2c2dc84550741f163d": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-15T10:50:12Z",
      "body": "The scheduler selected its gates before it measured the baseline, both at the\nstart and in the refresh inside the admission. A gate list that gained a\nblocking gate between the two ran as the old selection while every later\nsnapshot matched, and the run ended green. Now the selection is read again\nright after the baseline snapshot, and the refresh measures its baseline\nbefore it reloads the list; a later change moves the tree and is refused or\nrefreshed. A seconds-only run still takes no snapshot.\n\nTests, red before the fix (tests/test_verify_before_admission.py):\n- test_selection_is_bound_to_the_measured_configuration\n- test_refreshed_selection_is_bound_to_the_measured_configuration\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "30bf06b4f8c96d6465f61a2c2dc84550741f163d",
      "subject": "fix(verify-cheap-before-admission): the gate selection is bound to the measured configuration (phase-6 row F6-2)",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/verify_run.py"
      ]
    },

    "36b4b356ca029bc73d971a6bef30a7331c1c944d": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-14T18:59:01Z",
      "body": "The tree baseline is measured only for a run with protected work - the one\ncase that reuses cheap results across the admission. A seconds-only job\n(docs, drift) and a cheap pass that ended blocking red rely on no baseline,\nso they no longer refuse over an unmeasurable or moving tree (L2-3, L2-8).\nEvery ending - green, red, refused, refused admission - goes through one\nfinish(): the refused run names the gates it did not run, prints a banner\nand closes its history record red (L2-2). The cheap phase's not-run header\nnames every blocking red gate instead of claiming a stop at the first\n(L2-7). A refusal names the paths that moved. The worker rule lives once in\nverify_run.worker_bound, used by the full and the targeted check (L2-6).\nThe gates' default interpreter comes from the env argument (L2-9).\n\nL2-1 is rejected: ruff and pytest self-ignore their caches; the new proof\ntest_real_tool_caches_keep_the_baseline_stable runs both inside a checkout\nwithout user-level excludes and stays stable.\n\nOrchestrator hand edit (Opus subagent, maintainer's word of 2026-11-14).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

    "7533598324c2aa390330623901d9d7e9f1609b6d": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-15T10:52:50Z",
      "body": "A SIGTERM after `Popen` created the gate but before its process group was\nregistered raised `GateInterrupted` before the cleanup existed, so the gate\nkept running and could keep the admission descriptor. `gate_process` now\nholds the run's signals back with temporary handlers (never\n`pthread_sigmask`, whose mask the child would inherit) from before `Popen`\nuntil inside the `try` whose `finally` ends the group, then delivers them;\nthe reader start sits inside that `try` too, and a reader that never started\nhas its pipe closed instead of joined.\n\nTest, red before the fix:\ntests/test_verify_before_admission.py::test_a_signal_at_the_launch_boundary_still_ends_the_gate\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "7533598324c2aa390330623901d9d7e9f1609b6d",
      "subject": "fix(verify-cheap-before-admission): a signal at the gate's launch boundary is deferred (phase-6 row F6-3)",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/verify_run.py"
      ]
    },

      "body": "Main brings the shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py, PR #416,\nbead coding-harness-bxxt.6), venv_guard (PR #415) and the journal citation\ngate (PR #418). The slip counter (bead coding-harness-bxxt.7) is carried into\nmain's structure; nothing of either side is reverted.\n\nConflict resolutions:\n\n- scripts/verify_duration.py: main's in-process writers stay (record_start,\n  record_gate, record_end with root, state_root and env). The slip counter's\n  comparison evidence is attached to them: record_start records\n  common_git_dir for its root, reads the runner-owned comparison variables\n  from the scheduler's env (_comparison_fields(env), falling back to the\n  process environment for the CLI), and creates the targeted history beside\n  the duration history under the same state root at the first version-2\n  marker. append_event/_open_history take both the slip counter's\n  `destination` (the targeted history) and main's keyword `state_root`;\n  targeted_history_path accepts a state root too. Imports keep both\n  Sequence and dataclass/field; _git and _gate_file_digest take main's form.\n  New COMPARISON_ENV_NAMES lists the three variables.\n- scripts/stage2.py: main's scheduler path stays the one full check. The\n  slip counter's single entry point full_verify(root, env, key, change,\n  prepare) is kept, now built on main's body: prepare runs first, outside\n  any admission (main's intent for the full-mode attempt), then\n  intent-to-add, then _scheduled_verify with\n  verify_duration.full_run_context(_checked_tree(root, change), change)\n  added to the scheduler's environment. verify_attempt's full mode hands its\n  preparation (format, cheap checks, ledger clearing, prepare_derived) to\n  full_verify as `prepare` instead of duplicating the intent-to-add,\n  scheduler and cleanup block (house rule 9: one path).\n- scripts/verify_run.py (no conflict, one addition): after recording the\n  start, run_verification drops the comparison variables from the gates'\n  environment, so a gate never inherits them and a check a gate starts is\n  never recorded as a second full run of the same change and tree.\n- tests/test_stage2.py: both sides' new tests kept. The slip end-to-end test\n  now uses the world's committed gate list instead of creating its own\n  decisions/ folder, and its `make` stub is the scheduler's protected gate:\n  it records nothing (the scheduler records start, gate and end) and fails if\n  it inherits the comparison context.\n- tests/test_verify_duration.py: the slip counter's version of the\n  derived-never-persisted test (the reader `slips` is exposed) replaces\n  main's deferral assertions; main's criterion-8 completion-context test is\n  kept.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",

    "942c683f3dc1b50a91ace30a1c79d3927f80f9b3": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-29T08:29:43Z",
      "body": "Omnigent's own tools reach a Claude Code session as mcp__omnigent__<tool>,\nand neither Claude Code's path rules nor the hooks on its file tools see\nthem. scripts/omnigent_policy.py now holds the one list (27 denied tools,\n17 allowed, the protected config path, a reason for each) and renders both\nlayers from it:\n\n- layer 1: permissions.deny in .claude/settings.json, one exact rule per\n  denied tool plus Edit(//**/.omnigent/config.yaml). It holds alone.\n- layer 2: tools/omnigent/policy.yaml, an Omnigent default policy with two\n  CEL policies, and tools/omnigent/install.sh, which merges it into the\n  maintainer's Omnigent config (backup, validation with Omnigent's own\n  parser, refuses without a terminal). It is built, not installed.\n\nThe CEL policy tests `in` over a literal list rather than `.exists(...)`:\ncelpy evaluates both sides of `&&`, and on an event without a tool name the\nmacro's chain of errors doubles its message at every element, which hangs\nthe evaluation at 27 tools. The offline tests run every odd event shape\nthrough Omnigent's cel_policy under a time limit.\n\nThe script has no CI caller by nature (the installer runs on the\nmaintainer's machine), so it is listed in ci_gates.OHNE_AUFRUFER.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HRfJHTtj6rvcgudkYjJoP7\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "942c683f3dc1b50a91ace30a1c79d3927f80f9b3",
      "subject": "feat(omnigent): deny Omnigent's writing tools by name, from one list",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/ci_gates.py",
        "scripts/omnigent_policy.py"
      ]
    },

    "9fcf3c224fd1676a006ca4b57c2fea9d17b00327": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-29T08:57:36Z",
      "body": "install.sh took the launcher's first line literally after \"#!\", so\n\"#!/usr/bin/env python3\" was rejected as \"Omnigent not found\", while\nscripts/omnigent_policy.py handled the env form. The installer now asks the\nmodule (--print-python), run by any python3: PyYAML is imported lazily so\nthe module loads on the standard library alone. The module's resolver also\nreads the \"#!/bin/sh\" + \"'''exec' <path>\" launcher form that carries a path\nwith spaces.\n\nTests: the three launcher forms and the failure cases, and the installer\nrun against a launcher that names \"env python3\" (red with the old script).\n\nReview finding F-3 of omnigent-deny-layers.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HRfJHTtj6rvcgudkYjJoP7\n",
      "body_truncated": false,

      "subject": "fix(omnigent): resolve Omnigent's interpreter in one place",

    "c8298ce9806045bd9f86ea6ab8df9714f20a564b": {

      "author_utc": "2026-10-30T13:44:32Z",
      "body": "Each admission publishes a random token with its ownership and hands it\nto its children through HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_TOKEN.       "author_utc": "2026-11-20T10:27:07Z",
      "body": "The orchestrator applies the held-path step of the plan, as the maintainer\ndecided on 2026-11-20:\n\n- model-endpoints.yaml declares the `spec_review` block the runner reads:\n  call limit 30 minutes, pause 30 seconds, fallback deepseek-v4.1-flash on\n  opencode-go (L3-2).\n- AGENTS.md and docs/WORKFLOW.md no longer call phase 2a optional; the class\n  table requires the review for bounded, feature and architectural changes;\n  the class paragraph says implement checks the class on every route; the\n  draft chain repeats draft and review up to round three, with the final\n  draft and the recorded fourth-round form; a new subsection states what\n  counts, currency, retry and fallback, the re-check and the inventory\n  (L2-8, L2-11, L3-3, L3-4). README's phase line follows.\n- prompts/02-spec.md and prompts/02a-spec-review.md state the re-review, the\n  strict severities and the exact `No finding.` answer (L3-6).\n- The handover skill runs `--spec-review-inventory` in the morning handover\n  (L3-10).\n- The criterion 1-3 tests read every workflow text and went red against the\n  old texts by hand; new tests anchor the prompt format, the repository's\n  declaration and the skill (L2-12, L3-5). The test world drops the real\n  `spec_review` block so fixtures declare their own.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",

          "excerpt": "def state_base() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"The state base the shared root hangs off; an inheriting child must keep this, not the root.\n\n    A child handed `XDG_STATE_HOME` pointing at the root itself would resolve\n    the next layer down (`.../coding-harness/coding-harness`) and read another\n    machine's state — so the environment a local child inherits names the base,\n    and both sides resolve the same root.\n    \"\"\"\n    base = os.environ.get(\"XDG_STATE_HOME\")\n    # A relative value is ignored, as the XDG base-directory rule says: it would resolve against each\n    # entry's own working directory and split the shared admission (review row L1-3).\n    return Path(base) if base and Path(base).is_absolute() else Path.home() / \".local\" / \"state\"\n",

          "excerpt": "### Night runs\n\nA night run works its queue alone and sequentially; two standing rules\n(maintainer, 2026-10-26; bead coding-harness-yuw.4) keep it moving where a\nday session would ask:\n\n1. **Codex at capacity:** wait four minutes and retry once. The step carries a note with the reason,\n   and the run continues. The runner automates this once bead\n   coding-harness-m98e lands.\n2. **A further case of the same mechanism at a phase-6 re-check:** record\n   the finding, park that pull request and continue with the next queue\n   item; the maintainer decides it in the morning.\n\n**The night profile (since the night-stall-guard change, 2026-11-09; bead\ncoding-harness-ibde).** An unattended session starts Claude Code through the\nnight launcher so a permission question cannot hold the run:\n`python3 ~/.claude/night.py` followed by the arguments a normal `claude` call\nwould take. The launcher reads the explicit ask and deny rules of the supported\nsettings scopes, turns every sourced ask rule into a deny in a private overlay,\nand runs `claude --settings <overlay> --permission-mode dontAsk` for this\ninvocation only; the day settings are never rewritten, and the overlay lives in\na temporary directory for the child's lifetime. A denied action therefore\nreturns control at once instead of waiting for a person: the session continues\nwith an authorised alternative, or parks the denied step and records it — it\nnever disables the brake to get through. The launch is refused before `claude`\nstarts when a present settings file cannot be read or parsed, or when a caller\nargument would replace the profile (`--settings`, `--permission-mode`,\n`--dangerously-skip-permissions`). What the profile does not cover stays as it\nis: external policy and authentication dialogs, a stopped or usage-limited\nsession, and — until the maintainer chooses a push service — no phone alert\nand no independent heartbeat exists.\n\n**The 30-minute wake (standing since 2026-11-05/06; bead\ncoding-harness-7x3c).** Supervision of an unattended run rests on scheduled\nreturns of control, not on session-only timers that die with their session\nand not on idle polling. A **wake** is a scheduled return of control to the\norchestrating session; elapsed time or a printed message alone does not\nestablish delivery. A **lane** is one worktree with the change it serves;\nthe run's a",

          "excerpt": "def inherit_env(env: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The environment a local check runs under, with the admission state it must carry.\n\n    This is additive and local-only: a runner's allowlist stays closed, foreign\n    calls receive none of these names, and a genuine inherited marker travels\n    so a nested check reuses its ancestor's admission even after local\n    environment filtering.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = dict(env)\n    env[\"XDG_STATE_HOME\"] = str(state_base())\n    if FLOOR_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[FLOOR_ENV] = os.environ[FLOOR_ENV]\n    # The slot setting travels to local children when present, so a nested\n    # runner's own protected work — never a nested entry, which parses\n    # nothing — sees the same configuration its parent had (criterion 2).\n    # The foreign-model environment allowlist stays closed to HARNESS_*.\n    if SLOTS_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[SLOTS_ENV] = os.environ[SLOTS_ENV]\n    nested = nested_holder_pid()\n    marker, token = (nested, os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV)) if nested is not None else (_active_pid(), _active_token())\n    if marker is not None and token:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(marker)\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = token\n    else:\n        env.pop(LOCK_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(TOKEN_ENV, None)\n    # The admission context resolves the same way the child itself would: its\n    # own active admission, an inherited one, or nothing (bead\n    # coding-harness-1um6). A fresh context travels so the child records the\n    # measured wait as its own; an inherited one does not travel — the child\n    # resolves the shared context from the validated ownership record instead.\n    # Never the token.\n    context = admission_context()\n    if context.admission_id is not None and context.reused is False:\n        env[ADMISSION_ID_ENV] = context.admission_id\n        if context.wait_seconds is not None:\n            env[ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV] = repr(context.wait_seconds)\n    else:\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_ID_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV, None)\n    return env\n",

          "excerpt": "def _spawn_child(\n    command: list[str], pass_fds: tuple[int, ...], admission: _Admission | None\n) -> subprocess.Popen[bytes]:\n    \"\"\"The protected command in its own session, stdout and stderr reaching the operator.\"\"\"\n    env = dict(os.environ)\n    if admission is not None:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(os.getpid())\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = admission.token\n        env[ADMISSION_ID_ENV] = admission.admission_id\n        if admission.wait_seconds is not None:\n            env[ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV] = repr(admission.wait_seconds)\n    else:\n        # A nested supervision inherits only the marker: the fresh context of\n        # an ancestor's admission must not pass itself off as this child's own.\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_ID_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV, None)\n    return subprocess.Popen(command, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEV",

          "excerpt": "def full_verify(\n    root: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str],\n    key: str | None,\n    change: str | None = None,\n    prepare: Callable[[], list[str]] | None = None,\n) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The full check through the shared two-phase scheduler: the problems, empty when it is green.\n\n    The one full check of the runner: a targeted route whose coverage was not safe, phase 6's\n    boundary and the full-mode attempt verification (whose `prepare` runs first, outside any\n    admission). The scheduler's environment carries the runner-owned comparison context\n    (`verify_duration.full_run_context`), so the run's start record can later be paired with a\n    targeted predecessor: the checked tree is captured after the intent-to-add entries, exactly\n    what the gates are handed (bead coding-harness-bxxt.7).\n    \"\"\"\n    problems: list[str] = []\n    intended: list[bytes] = []\n    try:\n        if prepare is not None:\n            preparation = prepare()\n            if preparation:\n                return preparation\n        try:\n            intended = intend_new_files(root, env)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return [f\"the attempt's new files could not be added intent-to-add before `make verify`: {error}\"]\n        scheduled_env = {**env, **verify_duration.full_run_context(_checked_tree(root, change), change)}\n        out_text, err_text, code = _scheduled_verify(root, scheduled_env, \"verify\")\n        if code != 0:\n            problems.append(f\"`make verify` exited {code}\\n{verify_evidence_text(out_text, err_text, key)}\".rstrip())\n    except verify_lock.VerifyLockError as error:\n        problems.append(scrub(f\"`make verify` could not complete: {error}\", key))\n    except StepTimedOut as error:\n        problems.append(f\"`make verify` did not finish: {error}\")\n    finally:\n        try:\n            drop_intended(root, intended, env)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            problems.append(f\"the attempt's intent-to-add entries could not be removed after `make verify`: {error}\")\n    return problems\n",

      "statement": "The one full check runs through `full_verify`, which goes through the shared two-phase scheduler `verify_run.run_verification`; the scheduler's default executor `gate_process` spawns each gate with `start_new_session=True` and its own live-group registration. The declared per-call bounds are `TOOL_SECONDS` (5 minutes), `VERIFY_SECONDS` (45 minutes) and `GIT_SECONDS` (2 minutes), with the targeted pytest step sharing `VERIFY_SECONDS`. A detached verify-bearing step therefore has to enter `run_verification` (not call `make` directly) and carry or relax these bounds."

          "excerpt": "def hold_admission(command: list[str]) -> Iterator[tuple[int, ...] | None]:\n    \"\"\"One machine admission around protected work: queue, memory gate, published ownership.\n\n    Yields the descriptors local children must inherit, or None when this\n    entry is nested in an ancestor's admission. A process that already holds\n    or is acquiring an independent admission is refused before any queueing.\n    Refusals raise VerifyLockRefused or MemoryFloorRefused before the body\n    runs; release happens in every ending, after any child cleanup the caller\n    does.\n    \"\"\"\n    inherited = nested_holder_pid()\n    if inherited is not None:\n        _log(f\"inheriting admission from pid {inherited}; no queue and no memory wait\")\n        yield None\n        return\n    with _independent_admission_guard():\n        setting = verify_slots_setting()\n        admission = _Admission(_prepare_state(), command, setting)\n        try:\n            admission.enter()\n        except BaseException:\n            admission.release()\n            raise\n        try:\n            yield admission.pass_fds()\n        finally:\n            admission.release()\n",

          "excerpt": "def inherit_env(env: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The environment a local check runs under, with the admission state it must carry.\n\n    This is additive and local-only: a runner's allowlist stays closed, foreign\n    calls receive none of these names, and a genuine inherited marker travels\n    so a nested check reuses its ancestor's admission even after local\n    environment filtering.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = dict(env)\n    env[\"XDG_STATE_HOME\"] = str(state_base())\n    if FLOOR_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[FLOOR_ENV] = os.environ[FLOOR_ENV]\n    # The slot setting travels to local children when present, so a nested\n    # runner's own protected work — never a nested entry, which parses\n    # nothing — sees the same configuration its parent had (criterion 2).\n    # The foreign-model environment allowlist stays closed to HARNESS_*.\n    if SLOTS_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[SLOTS_ENV] = os.environ[SLOTS_ENV]\n    nested = nested_holder_pid()\n    marker, token = (nested, os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV)) if nested is not None else (_active_pid(), _active_token())\n    if marker is not None and token:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(marker)\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = token\n    else:\n        env.pop(LOCK_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(TOKEN_ENV, None)\n    # The admission context resolves the same way the child itself would: its\n    # own active admission, an inherited one, or nothing (bead\n    # coding-harness-1um6). A fresh context travels so the child records the\n    # measured wait as its own; an inherited one does not travel — the child\n    # resolves the shared context from the validated ownership record instead.\n    # Never the token.\n    context = admission_context()\n    if context.admission_id is not None and context.reused is False:\n        env[ADMISSION_ID_ENV] = context.admission_id\n        if context.wait_seconds is not None:\n            env[ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV] = repr(context.wait_seconds)\n    else:\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_ID_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV, None)\n    return env\n",

          "excerpt": "def _spawn_child(\n    command: list[str], pass_fds: tuple[int, ...], admission: _Admission | None\n) -> subprocess.Popen[bytes]:\n    \"\"\"The protected command in its own session, stdout and stderr reaching the operator.\"\"\"\n    env = dict(os.environ)\n    if admission is not None:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(os.getpid())\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = admission.token\n        env[ADMISSION_ID_ENV] = admission.admission_id\n        if admission.wait_seconds is not None:\n            env[ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV] = repr(admission.wait_seconds)\n    else:\n        # A nested supervision inherits only the marker: the fresh context of\n        # an ancestor's admission must not pass itself off as this child's own.\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_ID_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV, None)\n    return subprocess.Popen(command, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEV",

          "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        elif not table:\n            raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        for line in table:\n            parts = line.split(None, 2)\n            if (\n                len(parts) != 3\n                or not parts[0].isdigit()\n                or not run_report.ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1])\n                or not parts[2].strip()\n            ):\n                raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        rows = run_report.parse_processes(raw, changes)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        lines.append(str(error))\n        return lines\n    if not rows:\n        if run_report.stage2 is not None:\n            lines.append(\"none matched\")\n        return lines\n    lines.extend(f\"pid {row.pid} · {row.label} · change {row.change} · elapsed {row.elapsed}\" for row in rows)\n    return lines\n",

          "excerpt": "def parse_processes(ps_text: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> list[ProcessRow]:\n    \"\"\"The runner invocations and verification processes of one `ps` table.\n\n    Token matching only: a string inside an unrelated command - a shell\n    wrapper, an editor, an echo - is discarded, never reported.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for line in ps_text.splitlines():\n        parts = line.split(None, 2)\n        if len(parts) < 3 or not parts[0].isdigit() or not ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1]):\n            continue  # the header line and anything unshaped\n        pid, elapsed, command = parts\n        tokens = command.split()\n        if not tokens:\n            continue\n        row = _stage2_row(tokens, pid, elapsed, changes) or _verify_row(tokens, pid, elapsed)\n        if row is not None:\n            rows.append(row)\n    return rows\n",

A hook must never hang a session start.\nrun_bounded() {\n  local secs=$1 sin=$2 sout=$3 serr=$4\n  shift 4\n  # A new process group contains the command and all descendants.           "excerpt": "### Night runs\n\nA night run works its queue alone and sequentially; two standing rules\n(maintainer, 2026-10-26; bead coding-harness-yuw.4) keep it moving where a\nday session would ask:\n\n1. **Codex at capacity:** wait four minutes and retry once. If the retry\n   fails too, Sonnet 5.5 takes that one step — a repair through\n   `stage2.py repair <change> --stage2-off \"<reason>\"`, a phase-6 review or\n   re-check through a read-only Sonnet 5.5 sub-agent whose rows the\n   orchestrator records unchanged. The step carries a note with the reason,\n   and the run continues. The runner automates this once bead\n   coding-harness-m98e lands.\n2. **A further case of the same mechanism at a phase-6 re-check:** record\n   the finding, park that pull request and continue with the next queue\n   item; the maintainer decides it in the morning.\n\n**The night profile (since the night-stall-guard change, 2026-11-09; bead\ncoding-harness-ibde).** An unattended session starts Claude Code through the\nnight launcher so a permission question cannot hold the run:\n`python3 ~/.claude/night.py` followed by the arguments a normal `claude` call\nwould take. The launcher reads the explicit ask and deny rules of the supported\nsettings scopes, turns every sourced ask rule into a deny in a private overlay,\nand runs `claude --settings <overlay> --permission-mode dontAsk` for this\ninvocation only; the day settings are never rewritten, and the overlay lives in\na temporary directory for the child's lifetime. A denied action therefore\nreturns control at once instead of waiting for a person: the session continues\nwith an authorised alternative, or parks the denied step and records it — it\nnever disables the brake to get through. The launch is refused before `claude`\nstarts when a present settings file cannot be read or parsed, or when a caller\nargument would replace the profile (`--settings`, `--permission-mode`,\n`--dangerously-skip-permissions`). What the profile does not cover stays as it\nis: external policy and authentication dialogs, a stopped or usage-limited\nsession, and — until the maintainer chooses a push service — no phone alert\nand no independent heartbeat exists.\n\n**The 30-minute wake (standing since 2026-11-05/06; bead\ncoding-harness-7x3c).** Supervision of an unattended run rests on scheduled\nreturns of control, not on session-only timers that die with their session\nand not on idle polling. A **wake** is a scheduled return of control to the\norchestrating session; elapsed time or a printed message alone does not\nestablish delivery. A **lane** is one worktree with the change it serves;\nthe run's active lanes — those with authorised work still eligible to run —\nform the watch list. Before a run enters unattended operation, its session\ncreates a run-specific state directory under\n`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/night/<run-id>/` holding\n`lanes.txt`, a `busy/` directory and an append-only `lane-watch.log`, so a\nsuccessor session can resume the run from the files without chat memory.\nChoose `<run-id>` as the UTC start date plus an unused letter, for example\n`2026-11-06-a`; concurrent runs on that date take different letters. Record\nthe run id and state-directory path in the run's handover file under\n`docs/journal/handover/<date>-<name>.md`. This is the record for parked\nquestions, completed-lane outcomes and the end reason throughout this\nroutine, not a change's `handover.md` or the session-notes safety net.\nA successor finds the run id in that handover and reuses its directory,\nnever creating a second directory for the resumed run. The state directory\nrecords the run's wake and keep-awake handles and busy-marker ownership;\na successor taking over that run uses this record to manage its resources,\nincluding handles started by the preceding session. A lane entry names the\nlane id, its worktree, the current item and the next authorised action, and is updated whenever the work changes. These files\nare session state: never a replacement tracker and never a",

          "excerpt": "def _stop_and_reap(proc, grace):\n    \"\"\"Terminate the child (its whole group when it has one), kill after the grace, reap.\"\"\"\n    group = _own_group(proc)\n    _signal_child(proc, signal.SIGTERM, group)\n    leader_exited = True\n    try:\n        proc.wait(timeout=grace)\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n        leader_exited = False\n    # After the grace the whole launched group is killed, also when the leader already exited on\n    # SIGTERM: a descendant that ignores SIGTERM must not outlive a cancellation (F-34). A group\n    # with no member left makes the call a no-op.\n    if group or not leader_exited:\n        _signal_child(proc, signal.SIGKILL, group)\n    if not leader_exited:\n        try:\n            proc.wait(timeout=max(grace, 5.0))\n        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:  # pragma: no cover - SIGKILL was sent to a live child\n            return \"\", \"\"\n    try:\n        return proc.communicate(timeout=max(grace, 1.0))\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n        return \"\", \"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def dispatch(\n    slots,\n    *,\n    gate: Callable[[Slot], GateVerdict],\n    launcher: Callable[[Slot, float], Any],\n    audit: Callable[[Slot, GateVerdict], None] | None = None,\n    on_terminal: Callable[[Slot, SlotResult], None] | None = None,\n    stop: threading.Event | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    reserve: float = 0.0,\n    clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,\n    per_provider_limit: int = PER_PROVIDER_LIMIT,\n    grace: float = 2.0,\n) -> DispatchResult:\n    \"\"\"Run one stage. Each slot ends with exactly one terminal outcome.\n\n    ``on_terminal(slot, result)`` is called once per slot, in the thread that set the outcome and\n    before that thread takes its next slot (launched, cancelled, refused and not-started slots\n    alike). An exception from it, or from ``audit`` carrying a ``stage_stop_reason`` attribute,\n    is a stage stop without a security refusal: queued slots are cancelled, running children\n    are stopped and reaped with their output kept, no further callback runs (the store it\n    writes to is the thing that failed) and the exit code is 1 unless a security refusal makes\n    it 2. The dispatcher knows nothing about what the callbacks write.\n    \"\"\"\n    stop = stop if stop is not None else threading.Event()\n    ordered = sorted(slots, key=lambda s: (not s.required, s.order))\n    queues: dict[str, deque] = {}\n    for slot in ordered:\n        queues.setdefault(slot.provider, deque()).append(slot)\n    gate_lock = threading.Lock()\n    results: dict[str, SlotResult] = {}\n    sequence: list[str] = []\n    security = threading.Event()\n    failure: list = []  # the first (reason, detail) of a failed callback\n    pending = threading.local()\n\n    def finish(slot, outcome, *, started=False, rc=None, out=\"\", err=\"\", record=None, allowance=None):\n        results[slot.slot_id] = SlotResult(\n            slot.slot_id, dict(slot.identity), slot.required, outcome, started, rc, out, err, record, allowance\n        )\n        if not hasattr(pending, \"slots\"):\n            pending.slots = []\n        pending.slots.append(slot)\n\n    failure_lock = threading.Lock()\n    reported: set[str] = set()\n\n    def stage_stop(exc):\n        with failure_lock:\n            if not failure:\n                reason = getattr(exc, \"stage_stop_reason\", None) or \"state-store-unwritable\"\n                failure.append((reason, f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\"))\n        stop.set()\n\n    def report_terminal():\n        \"\"\"Run the callback for each outcome this thread just set, before it takes another slot.\"\"\"\n        slots, pending.slots = getattr(pending, \"slots\", []), []\n        for slot in slots:\n            if slot.slot_id in reported:\n                continue\n            reported.add(slot.slot_id)\n            if on_terminal is None or failure:\n                continue\n            try:\n                on_terminal(slot, results[slot.slot_id])\n            except Exception as exc:\n                stage_stop(exc)\n\n    def remaining():\n        return None if",

          "end_line": 388,
          "excerpt": "def _stage2_row(tokens: list[str], pid: str, elapsed: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> ProcessRow | None:\n    script = next((i for i, token in enumerate(tokens) if _is_stage2_script(token)), None)\n    if script is None or script + 1 >= len(tokens) or tokens[script + 1] not in KNOWN_VERBS:\n        return None\n    if script != 0:\n        if not re.fullmatch(r\"python(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*)?\", Path(tokens[0]).name):\n            return None  # the executable owns the invocation, not a preceding argument\n        if any(not token.startswith(\"-\") or token in {\"-c\", \"-m\", \"--\"} for token in tokens[1:script]):\n            return None\n    verb = tokens[script + 1]\n    change = NOT_READ\n    arguments = iter(tokens[script + 2 :])\n    value_options = {\n        \"--model\",\n        \"--class\",\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        \"--seats\",\n        \"--handover\",\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        \"--reason\",\n        \"--root\",\n    }\n    for token in arguments:\n        if token == \"--stage2-off\":\n            # Its reason is optional. A known change or another option must\n            # remain available to the positional/option reader below.\n            following = next(arguments, None)\n            if following is None:\n                break\n            if following not in changes and not following.startswith(\"-\"):\n                continue  # the explicit reason\n            token = following\n        if token in value_options:\n            next(arguments, None)\n            continue\n        if token.startswith(\"-\"):\n            continue  # options may stand between the verb and the change\n        if token in changes:\n            change = token\n        break  # only the first non-option token can name the change\n    return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=verb, change=change)\n",

          "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        elif not table:\n            raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        for line in table:\n            parts = line.split(None, 2)\n            if (\n                len(parts) != 3\n                or not parts[0].isdigit()\n                or not run_report.ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1])\n                or not parts[2].strip()\n            ):\n                raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        rows = run_report.parse_processes(raw, changes)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        lines.append(str(error))\n        return lines\n    if not rows:\n        if run_report.stage2 is not None:\n            lines.append(\"none matched\")\n        return lines\n  ",

          "citation": "prompts/01-explore.md::Phase 1 · Explore",
          "end_line": 69,
          "excerpt": "# Phase 1 · Explore\n\n**Model:** GLM 5.3 Flash — much input, little output, no deep reasoning needed;\nthrough `python3 scripts/stage2.py explore <change>` and its leak check\n(`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). When Stage 2 is off or Z.ai is unavailable, rerun as\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py explore <change> --stage2-off [REASON]`; Haiku 5.5\nexplores and the reason is recorded. A leak-check BLOCK stops; it never falls\nback.\n**Result:** `plans/changes/<name>/research.md`\n**Gate:** `research-handoff` (a complete swarm run is blocked until the research questions and neighbours are answered; see below).\n\n**Routing by class (ADR 0020).** A `feature` or `architectural` change\nexplores through the research swarm; a `bounded` change or a `spike` through\nthe single GLM 5.3 Flash explorer. The runner reads the class wherever stated:\nthe explore-only `--class` argument and the headers of `research.md` and\n`spec.md`. All available declarations must agree; missing, invalid or\ndisagreeing declarations refuse before any model call. `--stage2-off [REASON]`\nkeeps the Haiku 5.5 route and skips the class.\n\n**The swarm in one pass.** A finder trio (three seats, the same input) lists\nwhere things are: files and functions, applicable rules and ADRs, tests and\ngates, neighbouring specs. An Opus map merge keeps the exact union of those\nlists. Then eleven topics follow: the repository seats work eight (1-8) on that\nmap and the online seats three public ones (9-11), each model on the same brief\nand the same perspectives; a fresh Opus 5.5 context judges. The online topics see one\nfiltered public sentence and no repository content. That makes `39 + 3N`\ncalls for `N` selected free models; a topic report that fails its format gets\nat most one correction call from the same seat, so a run makes at most\n`72 + 6N` calls. The free models work the online topics only and are\nbest-effort. The judge holds evidence authority only: it\nexposes support, dissent, gaps and human questions, and decides no design and\nno workflow question. Only the runner writes `research.md`.\n\n**Required header: `neighbours:`.** The header of `research.md` carries a\n`neighbours:` list of the neighbouring specs you already know (paths to a\n`spec.md` of an active change, an archived change or a living spec). An empty\nlist is stated as `neighbours: []`; a missing header refuses the swarm. The\nrunner adds the neighbours the finders suggest; topic 5 reports on both kinds.\n\n**Steps, in this order, in the main conversation.**\n\n1. `python3 scripts/stage2.py prepare-explore <change> [--class CLASS]` refreshes\n   the Go model catalog, probes reachability, fills the six seats (a substitute\n   is named as such) and prints the selection report with a receipt id.\n2. Show that report to the maintainer unchanged. The receipt is single-use and\n   expires.\n3. `python3 scripts/stage2.py explore <change> --availability-reported <id>`\n   consumes the receipt and runs the swarm.\n\nIf a run is cut off (a quota or token limit, a kill), start steps 1 to 3 again:\nthe runner resumes — a finished contribution with the same inputs and prompt is\nreused, only the missing ones are called again. Do not edit tracked files\nbetween the runs. Only a complete run feeds phase 1a and phase 2; the gate\n`research-handoff` checks that the research questions and neighbours reached\nthe interview and the spec (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n\nYou collect facts about what exists today. You design nothing, you recommend\nnothing, you judge nothing.\n\nBefore writing anything: `rg` through `plans/specs/` and `plans/changes/` for the\ntopic. If a matching artefact exists, it is updated rather than created again.\n\n**Every statement names where it came from** — file and symbol, never a line\nnumber alone; line numbers age within the hour. What you have not read is\nwritten down as an open question, not as a guess. \"Not found\" and \"not there\"\nare two different statements and are written as two.\n\nStructure of `research.md`: what exists today · where it lives · what is unclea",

The runner automates this once bead\n   coding-harness-m98e lands.\n2. **A further case of the same mechanism at a phase-6 re-check:** record\n   the finding, park that pull request and continue with the next queue\n   item; the maintainer decides it in the morning.\n\n**The night profile (since the night-stall-guard change, 2026-11-09; bead\ncoding-harness-ibde).** An unattended session starts Claude Code through the\nnight launcher so a permission question cannot hold the run:\n`python3 ~/.claude/night.py` followed by the arguments a normal `claude` call\nwould take. The launcher reads the explicit ask and deny rules of the supported\nsettings scopes, turns every sourced ask rule into a deny in a private overlay,\nand runs `claude --settings <overlay> --permission-mode dontAsk` for this\ninvocation only; the day settings are never rewritten, and the overlay lives in\na temporary directory for the child's lifetime.           "excerpt": "def inherit_env(env: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The environment a local check runs under, with the admission state it must carry.\n\n    This is additive and local-only: a runner's allowlist stays closed, foreign\n    calls receive none of these names, and a genuine inherited marker travels\n    so a nested check reuses its ancestor's admission even after local\n    environment filtering.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = dict(env)\n    env[\"XDG_STATE_HOME\"] = str(state_base())\n    if FLOOR_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[FLOOR_ENV] = os.environ[FLOOR_ENV]\n    # The slot setting travels to local children when present, so a nested\n    # runner's own protected work — never a nested entry, which parses\n    # nothing — sees the same configuration its parent had (criterion 2).\n    # The foreign-model environment allowlist stays closed to HARNESS_*.\n    if SLOTS_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[SLOTS_ENV] = os.environ[SLOTS_ENV]\n    nested = nested_holder_pid()\n    marker, token = (nested, os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV)) if nested is not None else (_active_pid(), _active_token())\n    if marker is not None and token:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(marker)\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = token\n    else:\n        env.pop(LOCK_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(TOKEN_ENV, None)\n    # The admission context resolves the same way the child itself would: its\n    # own active admission, an inherited one, or nothing (bead\n    # coding-harness-1um6). A fresh context travels so the child records the\n    # measured wait as its own; an inherited one does not travel — the child\n    # resolves the shared context from the validated ownership record instead.\n    # Never the token.\n    context = admission_context()\n    if context.admission_id is not None and context.reused is False:\n        env[ADMISSION_ID_ENV] = context.admission_id\n        if context.wait_seconds is not None:\n            env[ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV] = repr(context.wait_seconds)\n    else:\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_ID_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV, None)\n    return env\n",

          "excerpt": "def hold_admission(command: list[str]) -> Iterator[tuple[int, ...] | None]:\n    \"\"\"One machine admission around protected work: queue, memory gate, published ownership.\n\n    Yields the descriptors local children must inherit, or None when this\n    entry is nested in an ancestor's admission. A process that already holds\n    or is acquiring an independent admission is refused before any queueing.\n    Refusals raise VerifyLockRefused or MemoryFloorRefused before the body\n    runs; release happens in every ending, after any child cleanup the caller\n    does.\n    \"\"\"\n    inherited = nested_holder_pid()\n    if inherited is not None:\n        _log(f\"inheriting admission from pid {inherited}; no queue and no memory wait\")\n        yield None\n        return\n    with _independent_admission_guard():\n        setting = verify_slots_setting()\n        admission = _Admission(_prepare_state(), command, setting)\n        try:\n            admission.enter()\n        except BaseException:\n            admission.release()\n            raise\n        try:\n            yield admission.pass_fds()\n        finally:\n            admission.release()\n",

          "excerpt": "### Night runs\n\nA night run works its queue alone and sequentially; two standing rules\n(maintainer, 2026-10-26; bead coding-harness-yuw.4) keep it moving where a\nday session would ask:\n\n1. **Codex at capacity:** wait four minutes and retry once. If the retry\n   fails too, Sonnet 5.5 takes that one step — a repair through\n   `stage2.py repair <change> --stage2-off \"<reason>\"`, a phase-6 review or\n   re-check through a read-only Sonnet 5.5 sub-agent whose rows the\n   orchestrator records unchanged. The step carries a note with the reason,\n   and the run continues. The runner automates this once bead\n   coding-harness-m98e lands.\n2. **A further case of the same mechanism at a phase-6 re-check:** record\n   the finding, park that pull request and continue with the next queue\n   item; the maintainer decides it in the morning.\n\n**The night profile (since the night-stall-guard change, 2026-11-09; bead\ncoding-harness-ibde).** An unattended session starts Claude Code through the\nnight launcher so a permission question cannot hold the run:\n`python3 ~/.claude/night.py` followed by the arguments a normal `claude` call\nwould take. A denied action therefore\nreturns control at once instead of waiting for a person: the session continues\nwith an authorised alternative, or parks the denie",

Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06).           "excerpt": "def dispatch(\n    slots,\n    *,\n    gate: Callable[[Slot], GateVerdict],\n    launcher: Callable[[Slot, float], Any],\n    audit: Callable[[Slot, GateVerdict], None] | None = None,\n    on_terminal: Callable[[Slot, SlotResult], None] | None = None,\n    stop: threading.Event | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    reserve: float = 0.0,\n    clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,\n    per_provider_limit: int = PER_PROVIDER_LIMIT,\n    grace: float = 2.0,\n) -> DispatchResult:\n    \"\"\"Run one stage. Each slot ends with exactly one terminal outcome.\n\n    ``on_terminal(slot, result)`` is called once per slot, in the thread that set the outcome and\n    before that thread takes its next slot (launched, cancelled, refused and not-started slots\n    alike). An exception from it, or from ``audit`` carrying a ``stage_stop_reason`` attribute,\n    is a stage stop without a security refusal: queued slots are cancelled, running children\n    are stopped and reaped with their output kept, no further callback runs (the store it\n    writes to is the thing that failed) and the exit code is 1 unless a security refusal makes\n    it 2. The dispatcher knows nothing about what the callbacks write.\n    \"\"\"\n    stop = stop if stop is not None else threading.Event()\n    ordered = sorted(slots, key=lambda s: (not s.required, s.order))\n    queues: dict[str, deque] = {}\n    for slot in ordered:\n        queues.setdefault(slot.provider, deque()).append(slot)\n    gate_lock = threading.Lock()\n    results: dict[str, SlotResult] = {}\n    sequence: list[str] = []\n    security = threading.Event()\n    failure: list = []  # the first (reason, detail) of a failed callback\n    pending = threading.local()\n\n    def finish(slot, outcome, *, started=False, rc=None, out=\"\", err=\"\", record=None, allowance=None):\n        results[slot.slot_id] = SlotResult(\n            slot.slot_id, dict(slot.identity), slot.required, outcome, started, rc, out, err, record, allowance\n        )\n        if not hasattr(pending, \"slots\"):\n            pending.slots = []\n        pending.slots.append(slot)\n\n    failure_lock = threading.Lock()\n    reported: set[str] = set()\n\n    def stage_stop(exc):\n        with failure_lock:\n            if not failure:\n                reason = getattr(exc, \"stage_stop_reason\", None) or \"state-store-unwritable\"\n                failure.append((reason, f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\"))\n        stop.set()\n\n    def report_terminal():\n        \"\"\"Run the callback for each outcome this thread just set, before it takes another slot.\"\"\"\n        slots, pending.slots = getattr(pending, \"slots\", []), []\n        for slot in slots:\n            if slot.slot_id in reported:\n                continue\n            reported.add(slot.slot_id)\n            if on_terminal is None or failure:\n                continue\n            try:\n                on_terminal(slot, results[slot.slot_id])\n            except Exception as exc:\n                stage_stop(exc)\n\n    def remaining():\n        return None if deadline is None else deadline - reserve - clock()\n\n    def out_of_time():\n        left = remaining()\n        return left is not None and left <= 0\n\n    def launch_next(queue):\n        \"\"\"Pop, gate, audit and launch under the one lock; return (slot, proc, allowance) or None.\"\"\"\n        with gate_lock:\n            if not queue:\n                return \"done\"\n            # Required-first holds across providers (F-54): a free slot waits until every\n            # required slot of every provider has been taken from its queue.\n            if not queue[0].required and any(q and q[0].required for q in queues.values()):\n                return \"wait\"\n            slot = queue.popleft()\n            sequence.append(slot.slot_id)\n            if stop.is_set():\n                finish(slot, \"cancelled\")\n                return None\n            if out_of_time():\n                finish(slot, \"not-started-deadline\")\n                return None\n            try:\n                verdict = gate(slot)\n           ",

          "end_line": 464,
          "excerpt": "def parse_processes(ps_text: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> list[ProcessRow]:\n    \"\"\"The runner invocations and verification processes of one `ps` table.\n\n    Token matching only: a string inside an unrelated command - a shell\n    wrapper, an editor, an echo - is discarded, never reported.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for line in ps_text.splitlines():\n        parts = line.split(None, 2)\n        if len(parts) < 3 or not parts[0].isdigit() or not ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1]):\n            continue  # the header line and anything unshaped\n        pid, elapsed, command = parts\n        tokens = command.split()\n        if not tokens:\n            continue\n        row = _stage2_row(tokens, pid, elapsed, changes) or _verify_row(tokens, pid, elapsed)\n        if row is not None:\n            rows.append(row)\n    return rows\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/run_report.py",
          "reference": "parse_processes",
          "start_line": 446,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },

          "end_line": 410,
          "excerpt": "def test_process_filter_emits_only_permitted_fields(tmp_path: Path, capsys) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Fault: an option hides a supported runner invocation, a substring match adds unrelated\n    processes, or command arguments beyond pid, label, change and elapsed leak (spec criterion 8).\"\"\"\n    root = tmp_path\n    make_change(root, \"run-report\", plan=plan_text(), findings=\"\")\n    listing = ps_output(\n        \"    1 00:01:02 python3 scripts/stage2.py implement run-report\",\n        \"    2 00:02:03 python3 scripts/stage2.py implement --stage2-off reason run-report\",\n        \"    3 00:30:00 make verify\",\n        \"    4 1-02:03:04 bash scripts/verify_all.sh\",\n        \"    9 00:00:10 python3 scripts/stage2.py draft run-report\",\n        \"    5 00:01:00 vim scripts/stage2.py implement\",  # an editor, not an invocation\n        \"    6 00:01:00 bash -c make verify\",  # a shell wrapper\n        \"    7 00:01:00 tail -f scripts/stage2.py\",  # a reader of the file\n        \"    8 00:10:00 echo SENTINEL-COMMAND run-report\",  # an unrelated command\n    )\n    run = fake_run({PS_ARGV: listing})\n    proc = proc_fixture(tmp_path)\n    code, out = run_main(root, capsys, run=run, proc_dir=proc)\n    assert code == 0\n    live = \"\\n\".join(blocks(out)[\"live\"])\n    for row in [\n        \"pid 1 · implement · change run-report · elapsed 00:01:02\",\n        \"pid 2 · implement · change run-report · elapsed 00:02:03\",  # the option hides nothing\n        \"pid 3 · verify · change not read · elapsed 00:30:00\",\n        \"pid 4 · verify · change not read · elapsed 1-02:03:04\",\n        \"pid 9 · draft · change run-report · elapsed 00:00:10\",\n    ]:\n        assert f\"    {row}\" in live\n    for absent in (\"pid 5\", \"pid 6\", \"pid 7\", \"pid 8\", \"vim\", \"tail\", \"echo\", \"SENTINEL-COMMAND\", \"--stage2-off\"):\n        assert absent not in live\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "tests/test_run_report.py",
          "reference": "test_process_filter_emits_only_permitted_fields",
          "start_line": 380,
          "supported": true,

        },

          "end_line": 256,
          "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        el",
