          "excerpt": "## Alternatives\n\nWho starts the weekly run, how the agent's work reaches GitHub, and how two\noperating-system users hand files to each other:\n\n- **(a) One orchestrator run as the maintainer, Hermes one-shot through a\n  sudo rule.** A weekly LaunchAgent of the maintainer runs\n  `scripts/research_recheck.py run`: it stages the note, runs\n  `sudo -n -u _chhermes <installed wrapper> <run dir>`, reads the agent's\n  event stream from the wrapper's standard output, checks the diff and\n  publishes. Consequences: the three steps are one process in one order, so\n  a sleeping laptop delays the run but cannot reorder it; one record per\n  run; the wall time is bounded by the orchestrator; no gateway is running\n  between runs. Owed: a sudo rule on the laptop that lets the maintainer\n  run one root-owned wrapper as the service user — a privilege reduction,\n  but a file in `/etc/sudoers.d/`. The spike's S-3 and S-6 prove adhd-\n  relief's gateway, not this path; the Coding Harness part has to prove\n  the one-shot path itself (S-2 already uses one-shot runs).\n- **(b) Hermes's gateway and its cron under the service user.** A\n  LaunchDaemon keeps the gateway running; a `hermes cron` job runs the\n  agent; the maintainer's prepare and publish jobs run at fixed offsets\n  before and after it. Consequences: the path adhd-relief's spike proves\n  (S-3, S-6); but three schedules must agree across a sleeping laptop,\n  the result files are mode 600 and the service user's (`research.md`\n  4.4), so the publish job needs a reader running as that user, and an\n  always-on process with a messaging surface runs for a job of minutes a\n  week.\n- **(c) A launchd chain without sudo.** Three jobs linked by queue\n  directories: the maintainer's prepare job fills an inbox, a LaunchDaemon\n  of the service user runs the agent when the inbox is not empty, and the\n  maintainer's publish job runs when the outbox fills. Consequences: no\n  sudo rule; but three jobs, three logs, and a half-finished run is spread\n  over two users' directories with no single record of what happened.\n- **(d) No unattended runner: the prompt by hand in Claude Code.** The\n  assessment's option A. Consequences: nothing to install and a first-party\n  model; but the job runs only when someone remembers, and the maintainer\n  chose Hermes (decisions, given). It stays the by-hand path the\n  runner-neutral prompt allows.\n\nChosen: **(a)**, because one process in one order removes the timing and\nhand-over questions of (b) and (c), keeps the wall-time cap and the record\nin fixed code the maintainer owns, and starts no always-on process.           "excerpt": "## Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall\n\nasked: 2026-11-09\nanswer: \"Ja\" — the change ships, in this order: (1) a night settings profile in which every rule that would ask the maintainer denies instead, so a call returns at once and the orchestrator takes another path; (2) a precise merge brake that asks (by day) or denies (at night) only for real merges — `gh pr merge`, the REST merge endpoint and the GraphQL mutations that merge or enqueue — while a read query that only names merge fields passes; (3) the phone alert for an open permission prompt and for a missing heartbeat comes after (1) and (2), as the second safeguard. The push service for (3) is not chosen yet and is asked when (3) is built.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: on 2026-11-08 at 22:26 UTC a read-only `gh api graphql` status query that named the fields mergedAt and isInMergeQueue matched the ask rule `Bash(gh api *merge*)` in .claude/settings.json; the orchestrating session waited for approval until 06:04 UTC and every heartbeat, watchdog wake-up and task notification queued behind it (session transcript), so finished lanes idled about 5.5 hours.\n  Intention: no single question may hold the night; the maintainer asked first how to stop the blocking at all (\"Wie kann ich es erstmal verhindern dass überhaupt alle Prozesse blockiert werden\").\n  Today: ask rules wait without limit; nothing alerts the maintainer; the watchdog only wakes the chat, which cannot act while a prompt is open.\n  Repository change: a night profile under tools/claude-code/ (installed by tools/claude-code/install.sh), narrowed merge rules in .claude/settings.json with tests of the rule set; the alert later.\n  Architecture change: none; moving each heartbeat into its own headless, time-limited call (launchd) belongs to the harness-neutral night-run work, not to this change.\n\nIn the context of the night run, whose orchestration lives in one chat that a\nsingle open permission prompt can hold for hours, facing ask rules that wait\nwithout limit and a merge brake that matched a read-only status query, we\ndecided to deny instead of ask at night and to narrow the merge brake to real\nmerges first, and to add a phone alert afterwards, to achieve that no question\ncan stop the night again, accepting that a denied call at night fails at once\nand the orchestrator must take another path — 2026-11-09\n",

          "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **Protected work:** gate execution through `scripts/verify_all.sh`, runner\n  post-run `make verify` in both `verify_attempt` and `verify_draft`, and\n  existing runner pytest checks in `red_first` and `fixed_test_proof`, including\n  the former's pytest import probe. Listings execute no protected work.\n- **Admission:** queue waiting followed by the memory check while holding the\n  exclusive lock, before protected work starts.\n- **Shared state:** `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/`, shared\n  by cooperating entries of the same user on this machine. The exclusive\n  lock is `verify.lock`; neither repository nor worktree identifies it.\n- **Nested work:** protected work descended from a lock holder, carrying\n  `HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_HELD=<holder-pid>` and `HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_TOKEN=<token>`,\n  the random token that admission published with its ownership. The token is\n  the proof of belonging: the environment reaches every descendant, also across\n  new sessions, nested runners and a dead holder, and no unrelated process\n  knows it (maintainer, 2026-10-30).\n\n",

          "excerpt": "6. When a protected invocation finishes, fails or is interrupted, remaining\n   live waiters can proceed without manual stale-lock or dead-waiter cleanup.\n   *Refuted by:* a dead holder/waiter blocking progress, or releasing ownership\n   while its protected child workload still runs.\n\n",

          "citation": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-06-verify-machine-lock/spec.md::Boundary",
          "end_line": 158,
          "excerpt": "## Boundary\n\nDecided by the maintainer on 2026-10-30 after repeated phase-6 rows on one\nmechanism (protected descendants outliving the admission). The admission\nprotects the machine's load, not data: an overlap of two checks costs time,\nnever correctness.\n\n- Covered: normal exit, failure, cancellation and trapped signals (SIGINT,\n  SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT) end the protected command's process group before\n  release; a grandchild left in that group after the command exits is ended\n  before release, by the supervisor and by the runner's timed launches. A trapped\n  signal that arrives while the protected command is being started is held back\n  until the command is registered for cleanup, in the supervisor as in the runner\n  (phase-6 row F6-9).\n- Accepted limit, signal timing (maintainer, 2026-10-30): after that deferral, a\n  further finding about the moment a signal arrives is an accepted limit, not a\n  finding: the lock protects the machine's load, never data.\n- Accepted limit: when an intermediate process is killed hard (SIGKILL) while\n  its own descendants run in another process group or session, those\n  descendants can outlive the admission and briefly overlap a successor. Their\n  time is bounded by the runner's step limits. A review row that describes\n  only this case is an accepted limit, not a finding.\n- A process container that would close the limit (cgroups, job objects) is out\n  of scope until the run report measures such overlaps in practice.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-06-verify-machine-lock/spec.md",
          "reference": "Boundary",
          "start_line": 134,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],
      "statement": "verify-machine-lock defines a machine-wide admission — a shared state root with an exclusive lock and memory floor, independent of repository or worktree — whose criterion 6 requires live waiters to proceed without manual cleanup and forbids releasing ownership while protected child workload still runs; its Boundary accepts as a limit that descendants in another process group or session can outlive the admission after a hard kill, their time bounded by the runner's step limits."

          "excerpt": "## Alternatives\n\nWho starts the weekly run, how the agent's work reaches GitHub, and how two\noperating-system users hand files to each other:\n\n- **(a) One orchestrator run as the maintainer, Hermes one-shot through a\n  sudo rule.** A weekly LaunchAgent of the maintainer runs\n  `scripts/research_recheck.py run`: it stages the note, runs\n  `sudo -n -u _chhermes <installed wrapper> <run dir>`, reads the agent's\n  event stream from the wrapper's standard output, checks the diff and\n  publishes. Consequences: the three steps are one process in one order, so\n  a sleeping laptop delays the run but cannot reorder it; one record per\n  run; the wall time is bounded by the orchestrator; no gateway is running\n  between runs. Owed: a sudo rule on the laptop that lets the maintainer\n  run one root-owned wrapper as the service user — a privilege reduction,\n  but a file in `/etc/sudoers.d/`. The spike's S-3 and S-6 prove adhd-\n  relief's gateway, not this path; the Coding Harness part has to prove\n  the one-shot path itself (S-2 already uses one-shot runs).\n- **(b) Hermes's gateway and its cron under the service user.** A\n  LaunchDaemon keeps the gateway running; a `hermes cron` job runs the\n  agent; the maintainer's prepare and publish jobs run at fixed offsets\n  before and after it. Consequences: the path adhd-relief's spike proves\n  (S-3, S-6); but three schedules must agree across a sleeping laptop,\n  the result files are mode 600 and the service user's (`research.md`\n  4.4), so the publish job needs a reader running as that user, and an\n  always-on process with a messaging surface runs for a job of minutes a\n  week.\n- **(c) A launchd chain without sudo.** Three jobs linked by queue\n  directories: the maintainer's prepare job fills an inbox, a LaunchDaemon\n  of the service user runs the agent when the inbox is not empty, and the\n  maintainer's publish job runs when the outbox fills. Consequences: no\n  sudo rule; but three jobs, three logs, and a half-finished run is spread\n  over two users' directories with no single record of what happened.\n- **(d) No unattended runner: the prompt by hand in Claude Code.** The\n  assessment's option A. Consequences: nothing to install and a first-party\n  model; but the job runs only when someone remembers, and the maintainer\n  chose Hermes (decisions, given). It stays the by-hand path the\n  runner-neutral prompt allows.\n\nChosen: **(a)**, because one process in one order removes the timing and\nhand-over questions of (b) and (c), keeps the wall-time cap and the record\nin fixed code the maintainer owns, and starts no always-on process. The\nchoice is a proposal; the merge of the ADR's pull request decides it.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When `python3 scripts/machine_facts.py` is invoked from a repository\n   worktree, it prints one machine-facts block freshly collected for that\n   invocation with a UTC date and time and labelled free-disk, swap,\n   registered-worktree and running-job fields.\n   *Refuted by:* a field or UTC stamp is missing, a stored snapshot is reused,\n   or a second invocation with changed fixtures repeats the previous values.\n\n2. When disk usage is readable, the free-disk field reports available space\n   on the filesystem containing the invoking worktree with an explicit unit\n   and that filesystem scope.\n   *Refuted by:* a fixture with different home and worktree volumes reports\n   home-volume space, reports used space as free, or omits the unit or scope.\n\n3. When swap usage is readable on macOS or Linux, the swap field reports\n   host-wide used and total swap with explicit units, including a readable\n   zero when no swap is configured.\n   *Refuted by:* used and total are confused, platform units are misconverted,\n   or a valid zero-total fixture is labelled unreadable.\n\n4. When Git's worktree list is readable, the worktree field reports the\n   number of registered non-bare worktrees for this repository.\n   *Refuted by:* a fixture containing a main checkout, linked and stale\n   registrations, a bare entry and paths with whitespace yields the wrong\n   count or counts unrelated filesystem directories.\n\n5. When the process table and shared job definitions are readable, the\n   running-job field lists each matched runner or verification invocation with process identifier,\n   elapsed time, verb and change attribution where known, or explicitly says\n   that none matched.\n   *Refuted by:* a matched process disappears, an unrelated wrapper or quoted\n   command becomes a job, an unknown change becomes a guessed name, or raw\n   command arguments appear in the block.\n\n6. If an individual source is unavailable, malformed or times out, its\n   affected field says `not read` with a bounded source-specific reason while\n   independently readable fields remain available and a valid command\n   invocation exits zero.\n   *Refuted by:* a failed source becomes zero or “none”, suppresses independent\n   facts, exposes raw diagnostics, hangs on an unbounded subprocess, or\n   changes the snapshot into a failing admission check.\n\n7. While collecting the snapshot, the command only reads local facts and\n   prints them, without writing files, changing Git or tracker state,\n   contacting a network service, or starting, stopping, locking or admitting\n   work.\n   *Refuted by:* the invocation creates bytecode or a state file, runs a\n   mutation or network command, calls the tracker, or changes another job.\n\n8.           "end_line": 43,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall\n\nasked: 2026-11-09\nanswer: \"Ja\" — the change ships, in this order: (1) a night settings profile in which every rule that would ask the maintainer denies instead, so a call returns at once and the orchestrator takes another path; (2) a precise merge brake that asks (by day) or denies (at night) only for real merges — `gh pr merge`, the REST merge endpoint and the GraphQL mutations that merge or enqueue — while a read query that only names merge fields passes; (3) the phone alert for an open permission prompt and for a missing heartbeat comes after (1) and (2), as the second safeguard. The push service for (3) is not chosen yet and is asked when (3) is built.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: on 2026-11-08 at 22:26 UTC a read-only `gh api graphql` status query that named the fields mergedAt and isInMergeQueue matched the ask rule `Bash(gh api *merge*)` in .claude/settings.json; the orchestrating session waited for approval until 06:04 UTC and every heartbeat, watchdog wake-up and task notification queued behind it (session transcript), so finished lanes idled about 5.5 hours.\n  Intention: no single question may hold the night; the maintainer asked first how to stop the blocking at all (\"Wie kann ich es erstmal verhindern dass überhaupt alle Prozesse blockiert werden\").\n  Today: ask rules wait without limit; nothing alerts the maintainer; the watchdog only wakes the chat, which cannot act while a prompt is open.\n  Repository change: a night profile under tools/claude-code/ (installed by tools/claude-code/install.sh), narrowed merge rules in .claude/settings.json with tests of the rule set; the alert later.\n  Architecture change: none; moving each heartbeat into its own headless, time-limited call (launchd) belongs to the harness-neutral night-run work, not to this change.\n\nIn the context of the night run, whose orchestration lives in one chat that a\nsingle open permission prompt can hold for hours, facing ask rules that wait\nwithout limit and a merge brake that matched a read-only status query, we\ndecided to deny instead of ask at night and to narrow the merge brake to real\nmerges first, and to add a phone alert afterwards, to achieve that no question\ncan stop the night again, accepting that a denied call at night fails at once\nand the orchestrator must take another path — 2026-11-09\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-stall-guard/decisions.md",
          "reference": "Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall",

          "excerpt": "## Alternatives\n\nWho starts the weekly run, how the agent's work reaches GitHub, and how two\noperating-system users hand files to each other:\n\n- **(a) One orchestrator run as the maintainer, Hermes one-shot through a\n  sudo rule.** A weekly LaunchAgent of the maintainer runs\n  `scripts/research_recheck.py run`: it stages the note, runs\n  `sudo -n -u _chhermes <installed wrapper> <run dir>`, reads the agent's\n  event stream from the wrapper's standard output, checks the diff and\n  publishes. Consequences: the three steps are one process in one order, so\n  a sleeping laptop delays the run but cannot reorder it; one record per\n  run; the wall time is bounded by the orchestrator; no gateway is running\n  between runs. Owed: a sudo rule on the laptop that lets the maintainer\n  run one root-owned wrapper as the service user — a privilege reduction,\n  but a file in `/etc/sudoers.d/`. The spike's S-3 and S-6 prove adhd-\n  relief's gateway, not this path; the Coding Harness part has to prove\n  the one-shot path itself (S-2 already uses one-shot runs).\n- **(b) Hermes's gateway and its cron under the service user.** A\n  LaunchDaemon keeps the gateway running; a `hermes cron` job runs the\n  agent; the maintainer's prepare and publish jobs run at fixed offsets\n  before and after it. Consequences: the path adhd-relief's spike proves\n  (S-3, S-6); but three schedules must agree across a sleeping laptop,\n  the result files are mode 600 and the service user's (`research.md`\n  4.4), so the publish job needs a reader running as that user, and an\n  always-on process with a messaging surface runs for a job of minutes a\n  week.\n- **(c) A launchd chain without sudo.** Three jobs linked by queue\n  directories: the maintainer's prepare job fills an inbox, a LaunchDaemon\n  of the service user runs the agent when the inbox is not empty, and the\n  maintainer's publish job runs when the outbox fills. Consequences: no\n  sudo rule; but three jobs, three logs, and a half-finished run is spread\n  over two users' directories with no single record of what happened.\n- **(d) No unattended runner: the prompt by hand in Claude Code.** The\n  assessment's option A. Consequences: nothing to install and a first-party\n  model; but the job runs only when someone remembers, and the maintainer\n  chose Hermes (decisions, given). It stays the by-hand path the\n  runner-neutral prompt allows.\n\nChosen: **(a)**, because one process in one order removes the timing and\nhand-over questions of (b) and (c), keeps the wall-time cap and the record\nin fixed code the maintainer owns, and starts no always-on process. The\nchoice is a proposal; the merge of the ADR's pull request decides it.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When `python3 scripts/stage2.py session <change> --model <id>` runs in the\n   change's dedicated worktree, it accepts the declared supported model.\n   *Refuted by:* no session parser, or dispatch from the main checkout,\n   detached HEAD or a different root than the validated change.\n2. If a handover path resolves outside the validated worktree, it is refused.\n   *Refuted by:* traversal or a symlink sending outside-file text to a model.\n5. If the leak check cannot measure or finds a match, nothing is dispatched.\n   *Refuted by:* missing denylist or failed scan producing a terminal call\n   or an audit claiming a clean check.\n7. When dispatch succeeds, a findings audit names date, requested model,\n   endpoint, handover source and the measured file/commit/rule counts.\n   *Refuted by:* missing or invented counts, wrong model, lost prior findings\n   or an audit indistinguishable from a completed review verdict.\n8. If dispatch fails after clean preflight, the command returns failure and\n   records a failed dispatch rather than claiming an interactive model ran.\n   *Refuted by:* denied automation or terminal dispatch failure\n   returning success or leaving a success-only audit.\n   A missing CLI/terminal executable is a prerequisite refusal (exit 2).\n   Successful Terminal acceptance is exit 0, not a CLI-start acknowledgment;\n   a subsequent CLI/login/model failure is reported in the new window.\n9. When a supported model is launched, the terminal runs the official CLI\n   interactively with that model and the checked worktree as its directory.\n   *Refuted by:* a non-interactive Pi mode (`--print`, `--mode`),\n   `codex exec`, any `opencode` call, wrong cwd, automatic fallback, or a\n   runner waiting for the interactive session to terminate.\n10.           "citation": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-stall-guard/decisions.md::Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall",
          "end_line": 43,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall\n\nasked: 2026-11-09\nanswer: \"Ja\" — the change ships, in this order: (1) a night settings profile in which every rule that would ask the maintainer denies instead, so a call returns at once and the orchestrator takes another path; (2) a precise merge brake that asks (by day) or denies (at night) only for real merges — `gh pr merge`, the REST merge endpoint and the GraphQL mutations that merge or enqueue — while a read query that only names merge fields passes; (3) the phone alert for an open permission prompt and for a missing heartbeat comes after (1) and (2), as the second safeguard. The push service for (3) is not chosen yet and is asked when (3) is built.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: on 2026-11-08 at 22:26 UTC a read-only `gh api graphql` status query that named the fields mergedAt and isInMergeQueue matched the ask rule `Bash(gh api *merge*)` in .claude/settings.json; the orchestrating session waited for approval until 06:04 UTC and every heartbeat, watchdog wake-up and task notification queued behind it (session transcript), so finished lanes idled about 5.5 hours.\n  Intention: no single question may hold the night; the maintainer asked first how to stop the blocking at all (\"Wie kann ich es erstmal verhindern dass überhaupt alle Prozesse blockiert werden\").\n  Today: ask rules wait without limit; nothing alerts the maintainer; the watchdog only wakes the chat, which cannot act while a prompt is open.\n  Repository change: a night profile under tools/claude-code/ (installed by tools/claude-code/install.sh), narrowed merge rules in .claude/settings.json with tests of the rule set; the alert later.\n  Architecture change: none; moving each heartbeat into its own headless, time-limited call (launchd) belongs to the harness-neutral night-run work, not to this change.\n\nIn the context of the night run, whose orchestration lives in one chat that a\nsingle open permission prompt can hold for hours, facing ask rules that wait\nwithout limit and a merge brake that matched a read-only status query, we\ndecided to deny instead of ask at night and to narrow the merge brake to real\nmerges first, and to add a phone alert afterwards, to achieve that no question\ncan stop the night again, accepting that a denied call at night fails at once\nand the orchestrator must take another path — 2026-11-09\n",

          "excerpt": "## What exists today\n\n**The change folder at exploration time (2026-11-06).** The explorer\nreported only the research skeleton in `plans/changes/night-heartbeat/`.\nThat is a historical snapshot, not the current file list: the folder now\nalso holds decisions, spec, plan, findings and trial reference evidence.\nThe bead's description was **not read** by the explorer because its tools\ncould not access the shared Dolt tracker. Finding A.3 in `docs/research/2026-09-26-agent-sdk-and-formal-models.md` (\"Seam 4 — the recap lock\", lines 201–243; TLA+ module `RecapLock`, lines 608–666) shows the design assumption \"a lock only grows old once its holder is dead\" fails when a child call runs longer than five minutes (hung network call, laptop asleep): a waiter then steals a live lock and two writers run — severity MINOR. The note's fix options are recorded \"for a bead, not applied\" (line 239): *a heartbeat that touches the lock while the child runs, so that \"old\" means \"no sign of life\"*, an owner token the trap checks, and a bound on the child call. `tests/test_recap_lock.py` (docstring) covers the 2026-09-22 possession fix (bead `hit`, part 3), not the A.3 live-holder-with-backdated-lock case the note proposes at its lines 420–423.\n\n2. **The lane-watch heartbeat, planned and not built.** `docs/journal/handover/2026-11-01-five-lane-night.md` records: the maintainer's rule \"every lane is always served\" with \"a lane watch mechanism is bead coding-harness-5q2p\" (lines 62–63); five interview answers prepared for the 15:00 block (lines 117–119: where the lane record lives, who writes it, when it is checked, report or serve an idle lane, order with 4emv); and the folded design (lines 271–278): lane watch (5q2p) built together with lane planning (4emv) — \"the runner writes a lane diary per lane into a state file at every verb's start and end; it is checked at every runner end, in the status line and **by a 20-minute heartbeat**; an idle lane always starts its next backlog bead itself\".           "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair. Reason: a run's history cannot be reset, and asking each time stopped\n  lanes overnight.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "{\n  \"author_utc\": \"2026-11-16T06:07:34Z\",\n  \"body\": \"The plans-registry gate turns red when a bead is closed and its change\\nfolder is not archived (e.g. verify-cheap-first, verify-step-limit,\\nverify-tmp-cleanup). make archive moved every eligible folder to\\nplans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-<name>/ and regenerated plans/INDEX.md;\\nten folders with open or unrendered beads stay.\\n\\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Jh36RHbF3hnqxk6Byjw7wx\\n\",\n  \"body_truncated\": false,\n  \"hash\": \"469966ff34ba6d222ada1f5a570ea29f43427f48\",\n  \"subject\": \"chore(plans): archive 34 change folders whose beads are closed\",\n  \"touched_mapped_paths\": [\n    \"plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-heartbeat/plan.md\",\n    \"plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-heartbeat/spec.md\",\n    \"plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-machine-facts/spec.md\",\n    \"plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-stall-guard/decisions.md\",\n    \"plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-stall-guard/spec.md\"\n  ]\n}",

          "citation": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-stall-guard/decisions.md::Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall",
          "end_line": 43,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall\n\nasked: 2026-11-09\nanswer: \"Ja\" — the change ships, in this order: (1) a night settings profile in which every rule that would ask the maintainer denies instead, so a call returns at once and the orchestrator takes another path; (2) a precise merge brake that asks (by day) or denies (at night) only for real merges — `gh pr merge`, the REST merge endpoint and the GraphQL mutations that merge or enqueue — while a read query that only names merge fields passes; (3) the phone alert for an open permission prompt and for a missing heartbeat comes after (1) and (2), as the second safeguard. The push service for (3) is not chosen yet and is asked when (3) is built.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: on 2026-11-08 at 22:26 UTC a read-only `gh api graphql` status query that named the fields mergedAt and isInMergeQueue matched the ask rule `Bash(gh api *merge*)` in .claude/settings.json; the orchestrating session waited for approval until 06:04 UTC and every heartbeat, watchdog wake-up and task notification queued behind it (session transcript), so finished lanes idled about 5.5 hours.\n  Intention: no single question may hold the night; the maintainer asked first how to stop the blocking at all (\"Wie kann ich es erstmal verhindern dass überhaupt alle Prozesse blockiert werden\").\n  Today: ask rules wait without limit; nothing alerts the maintainer; the watchdog only wakes the chat, which cannot act while a prompt is open.\n  Repository change: a night profile under tools/claude-code/ (installed by tools/claude-code/install.sh), narrowed merge rules in .claude/settings.json with tests of the rule set; the alert later.\n  Architecture change: none; moving each heartbeat into its own headless, time-limited call (launchd) belongs to the harness-neutral night-run work, not to this change.\n\nIn the context of the night run, whose orchestration lives in one chat that a\nsingle open permission prompt can hold for hours, facing ask rules that wait\nwithout limit and a merge brake that matched a read-only status query, we\ndecided to deny instead of ask at night and to narrow the merge brake to real\nmerges first, and to add a phone alert afterwards, to achieve that no question\ncan stop the night again, accepting that a denied call at night fails at once\nand the orchestrator must take another path — 2026-11-09\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-stall-guard/decisions.md",
          "reference": "Q-1 · How the change prevents a night stall",
          "start_line": 24,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-16-night-stall-guard/spec.md::Non-goals",
          "end_line": 122,
          "excerpt": "## Non-goals\n\n- The phone alert, permission-prompt monitoring and missing-heartbeat alert:\n  return after these safeguards, when the maintainer chooses the push service.\n- A scheduler, daemon, headless heartbeat architecture, automatic restart,\n  lane planner, runner process watchdog, dashboard or notification service.\n- Changing merge authority, approving a merge, bypassing another permission\n  system, or changing permissions of Codex, Pi or Omnigent itself.\n- Implementing the response to a denied call in `scripts/stage2.py`.\n- Phase 2b and an ADR: this bounded change configures the existing permission\n  boundary without changing the architecture, as the answered interview states.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "{\n  \"author_utc\": \"2026-10-09T13:56:58Z\",\n  \"body\": \"Work package 4 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi.           "end_line": 8207,
          "excerpt": "def test_a_timeout_kills_the_whole_process_group(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"O188-4: a grandchild of the stopped step does not survive.\"\"\"\n    # Planted fault: a timed-out group's descendant survives, or the post-kill drain is unbounded.\n    pidfile = tmp_path / \"grandchild.pid\"\n    handed: list[float | None] = []  # every timeout a communicate was given, the drain's included\n    known: list[int] = []  # the grandchild's PID once complete, so cleanup can always reach it\n    real_popen = subprocess.Popen\n\n    def popen(command, *args, **kwargs):\n        process = real_popen(command, *args, **kwargs)\n        real_communicate = process.communicate\n\n        def communicate(timeout=None):\n            handed.append(timeout)\n            if len(handed) == 1:\n                # Readiness, not a race: the grandchild's complete PID is held before the expiry is injected.\n                pid = _await_complete_pid(pidfile, 200)\n                assert pid is not None, \"the timed step never wrote its grandchild's complete pid\"\n                known.append(pid)\n                raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(command, timeout)\n            return real_communicate(timeout=timeout)  # the bounded drain on the really killed group\n\n        process.communicate = communicate  # type: ignore[method-assign]\n        return process\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, \"Popen\", popen)\n    # The record is written to a temporary file and renamed into place: the name appears only complete.\n    staged = f\"{pidfile}.tmp\"\n    try:\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.CallFailed, match=\"stopped by\"):\n            stage2.launch(\n                [\"bash\", \"-c\", f\"sleep 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > {staged} && mv {staged} {pidfile}; wait\"],\n                tmp_path,\n                {**os.environ},\n                timeout=1,\n                limit=\"the test limit\",\n            )\n        assert handed[0] == 1, \"the step was handed more than its allowance\"\n        assert handed[1] == stage2.KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS, \"the kill's drain is unbounded\"\n        (pid,) = known\n        for _ in range(100):  # watchdog only: the kill is delivered at once, the exit is reaped a moment later\n            if not _child_alive(pid):\n                return\n            time.sleep(0.02)\n        pytest.fail(\"the grandchild of the timed-out step is still running\")\n    finally:\n        # cleanup: every known PID is killed; a missing or already dead one is tolerated\n        _kill_known(known[0] if known else _complete_pid(pidfile))\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_timed_launch_ends_a_lingering_grandchild_before_returning(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    # Row F6-5 (re-check) of the machine lock. Planted fault: a runner check returned while a\n    # grandchild with closed descriptors and redirected output kept running, and the admission\n    # context released around it; only the supervisor ended a lingering group.\n    out = tmp_path / \"grandchild.pid\"\n    body = (\n        \"import subprocess, sys, pathlib; \"\n        \"g = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', 'import time; time.sleep(30)'], \"\n        \"stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL); \"\n        f\"pathlib.Path({str(out)!r}).write_text(str(g.pid))\"\n    )\n    done = stage2.launch([sys.executable, \"-c\", body], tmp_path, dict(os.environ), timeout=60)\n    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stderr\n    grandchild = int(out.read_text())\n    try:\n        deadline = time.monotonic() + 10.0  # watchdog only: bounds a wedged reap, never a verdict\n        alive = True\n        while alive and time.monotonic() < deadline:\n            try:\n                os.kill(grandchild, 0)\n            except ProcessLookupError:\n                alive = False\n            else:\n                time.sleep(0.1)\n        assert not alive, \"the launch returned while its grandchild still ran\"\n    finally:\n        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):\n            os.kill(grandchild, signal.SIGKILL)\n",

          "excerpt": "def _stage2_row(tokens: list[str], pid: str, elapsed: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> ProcessRow | None:\n    script = next((i for i, token in enumerate(tokens) if _is_stage2_script(token)), None)\n    if script is None or script + 1 >= len(tokens) or tokens[script + 1] not in KNOWN_VERBS:\n        return None\n    if script != 0:\n        if not re.fullmatch(r\"python(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*)?\", Path(tokens[0]).name):\n            return None  # the executable owns the invocation, not a preceding argument\n        if any(not token.startswith(\"-\") or token in {\"-c\", \"-m\", \"--\"} for token in tokens[1:script]):\n            return None\n    verb = tokens[script + 1]\n    change = NOT_READ\n    arguments = iter(tokens[script + 2 :])\n    value_options = {\n        \"--model\",\n        \"--class\",\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        \"--seats\",\n        \"--handover\",\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        \"--reason\",\n        \"--root\",\n    }\n    for token in arguments:\n        if token == \"--stage2-off\":\n            # Its reason is optional. A known change or another option must\n            # remain available to the positional/option reader below.\n            following = next(arguments, None)\n            if following is None:\n                break\n            if following not in changes and not following.startswith(\"-\"):\n                continue  # the explicit reason\n            token = following\n        if token in value_options:\n            next(arguments, None)\n            continue\n        if token.startswith(\"-\"):\n            continue  # options may stand between the verb and the change\n        if token in changes:\n            change = token\n        break  # only the first non-option token can name the change\n    return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=verb, change=change)\n",

          "excerpt": "def install() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Wrap every clock read in place; idempotent. Refuses when the runner is already imported.\n\n    A runner imported before the wrappers holds whatever it bound at import,\n    and an import-time read has already happened unseen, so the guard would\n    claim more than it checks.\n    \"\"\"\n    if _state[\"installed\"]:\n        return\n    early = _guarded_modules()\n    if early:\n        raise RuntimeError(f\"the runner was imported before the clock guard: {[m.__name__ for m in early]}\")\n    for name in sorted(TIME_CLOCK_ATTRS):\n        original = getattr(time, name)\n        ORIGINALS[f\"time.{name}\"] = original\n        WRAPPERS[f\"time.{name}\"] = _time_wrapper(name, original)\n    for name, positional in sorted(TIME_CONVERSION_ATTRS.items()):\n        original = getattr(time, name)\n        ORIGINALS[f\"time.{name}\"] = original\n        WRAPPERS[f\"time.{name}\"] = _conversion_wrapper(name, positional, original)\n    for key, wrapper in WRAPPERS.items():\n        setattr(time, key.removeprefix(\"time.\"), wrapper)\n    for name, owner in _DATETIME_OWNERS.items():\n        key = f\"{owner.__name__}.{name}\"\n        original = owner.__dict__[name]\n        ORIGINALS[key] = original\n        WRAPPERS[key] = _datetime_wrapper(owner, name, original)\n        _type_dict(owner)[name] = WRAPPERS[key]\n    for owner in (dt.date, dt.datetime):\n        ctypes.pythonapi.PyType_Modified(ctypes.py_object(owner))\n    _state[\"installed\"] = True\n    problems = installation_problems()\n    if problems:\n        raise RuntimeError(f\"the clock guard did not take effect: {problems}\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def runner_clock_reads() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Fail a test during which runner code read a machine clock outside `clock_now`.\"\"\"\n    problems = runner_clock_guard.installation_problems()\n    if problems:\n        pytest.fail(f\"the runner clock guard is not in effect: {problems}\")\n    bound = runner_clock_guard.unscanned_bound_reference_violations()\n    if bound:\n        pytest.fail(f\"the runner holds clock references bound past the guard: {bound}\")\n    unreported = runner_clock_guard.unreported_import_time_reads()\n    if unreported:\n        pytest.fail(\"runner code read a machine clock outside clock_now at import: \" + \"; \".join(map(str, unreported)))\n    start = len(runner_clock_guard.READS)\n    with runner_clock_guard.in_test():\n        yield\n    new = runner_clock_guard.READS[start:]\n    if new:\n        pytest.fail(\"runner code read a machine clock outside clock_now: \" + \"; \".join(map(str, new)))\n",

          "excerpt": "## How a test is written\n\n- **Stand-ins, never live calls.** A test that drives the runner puts small\n  programs on `PATH` in place of the model tools. They record their\n  arguments, environment and input, print canned output and contact nothing.\n  Credentials are synthetic. No test reads the maintainer's denylist, secrets\n  or loop records.\n- **Each new test names its fault.** Its docstring says which fault the test\n  was red on (`Planted fault: …`); this is the convention for new tests, and\n  older ones are not all rewritten. A test that has never been red is a test of\n  nothing.\n- **Doctrine tests.** Some tests read the workflow's own documents and prompts\n  and pin a rule there. Each one checks its fault on a planted copy of the\n  text, so the test is shown to catch the drift it guards.\n- **Mutation names.** A test that proves a gate goes red carries the fact in\n  its name (`…_goes_red…`, `…_refuses…`, `…_is_caught…`). A name moves with a\n  rename, a comment does not. The gate ratchet counts these names.\n- **A test reads only what travels**, or it skips with its reason. Otherwise\n  the kit probe turns it red in a repository that lacks the file.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/testing.md",
          "reference": "How a test is written",
          "start_line": 37,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },

          "citation": "docs/testing.md::What this does not prove",
          "end_line": 96,
          "excerpt": "## What this does not prove\n\n- **Counts measure how much is checked, not how well.** A large suite can\n  still miss a fault nobody wrote down. Mutation testing of the scripts is\n  planned, not built.\n- **Stand-ins prove the runner's handling, not the models.** Whether a model\n  reviews or implements well is measured on real runs, not in the suite.\n- **A green run proves the named criteria.** What no criterion names, no\n  gate holds.\n- **The stop hook can be skipped.** The hosted `verify` job is the gate that\n  cannot.\n",
          "kind": "local",

A gate without one needs a reason in a list that may only shrink (rule RB-G4). An empty set is no result: every gate asserts that what it measured is not empty (rule RB-G7). | [Rule table](governance/regelwerk.md), `scripts/mutation_evidence.py`, `tests/test_ci.py` |\n| 5 | A locked environment | Each checkout builds its own `.venv` from a lock with a hash for every package. Pinned outside tools are tested as the real program against offline contracts, not as expected arguments. A local green means what a CI green means. | `requirements-ci.txt`, `make venv` |\n| 6 | The kit probe | The probe copies everything the kit manifest marks as mechanism into an empty repository and runs the tests there. This is how \"the workflow can be handed over\" becomes a run. | `scripts/kit/probe.py`, `scripts/kit/manifest.yaml` |\n\nLayer 1 is a trust rule against models.           "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        elif not table:\n            raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        for line in table:\n            parts = line.split(None, 2)\n            if (\n                len(parts) != 3\n                or not parts[0].isdigit()\n                or not run_report.ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1])\n                or not parts[2].strip()\n            ):\n                raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        rows = run_report.parse_processes(raw, changes)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        lines.append(str(error))\n        return lines\n    if not rows:\n        if run_report.stage2 is not None:\n            lines.append(\"none matched\")\n        return lines\n    lines.extend(f\"pid {row.pid} · {row.label} · change {row.change} · elapsed {row.elapsed}\" for row in rows)\n    return lines\n",

          "excerpt": "def _stage2_row(tokens: list[str], pid: str, elapsed: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> ProcessRow | None:\n    script = next((i for i, token in enumerate(tokens) if _is_stage2_script(token)), None)\n    if script is None or script + 1 >= len(tokens) or tokens[script + 1] not in KNOWN_VERBS:\n        return None\n    if script != 0:\n        if not re.fullmatch(r\"python(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*)?\", Path(tokens[0]).name):\n            return None  # the executable owns the invocation, not a preceding argument\n        if any(not token.startswith(\"-\") or token in {\"-c\", \"-m\", \"--\"} for token in tokens[1:script]):\n            return None\n    verb = tokens[script + 1]\n    change = NOT_READ\n    arguments = iter(tokens[script + 2 :])\n    value_options = {\n        \"--model\",\n        \"--class\",\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        \"--seats\",\n        \"--handover\",\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        \"--reason\",\n        \"--root\",\n    }\n    for token in arguments:\n        if token == \"--stage2-off\":\n            # Its reason is optional. A known change or another option must\n            # remain available to the positional/option reader below.\n            following = next(arguments, None)\n            if following is None:\n                break\n            if following not in changes and not following.startswith(\"-\"):\n                continue  # the explicit reason\n            token = following\n        if token in value_options:\n            next(arguments, None)\n            continue\n        if token.startswith(\"-\"):\n            continue  # options may stand between the verb and the change\n        if token in changes:\n            change = token\n        break  # only the first non-option token can name the change\n    return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=verb,",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_timeout_kills_the_whole_process_group(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"O188-4: a grandchild of the stopped step does not survive.\"\"\"\n    # Planted fault: a timed-out group's descendant survives, or the post-kill drain is unbounded.\n    pidfile = tmp_path / \"grandchild.pid\"\n    handed: list[float | None] = []  # every timeout a communicate was given, the drain's included\n    known: list[int] = []  # the grandchild's PID once complete, so cleanup can always reach it\n    real_popen = subprocess.Popen\n\n    def popen(command, *args, **kwargs):\n        process = real_popen(command, *args, **kwargs)\n        real_communicate = process.communicate\n\n        def communicate(timeout=None):\n            handed.append(timeout)\n            if len(handed) == 1:\n                # Readiness, not a race: the grandchild's complete PID is held before the expiry is injected.\n                pid = _await_complete_pid(pidfile, 200)\n                assert pid is not None, \"the timed step never wrote its grandchild's complete pid\"\n                known.append(pid)\n                raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(command, timeout)\n            return real_communicate(timeout=timeout)  # the bounded drain on the really killed group\n\n        process.communicate = communicate  # type: ignore[method-assign]\n        return process\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, \"Popen\", popen)\n    # The record is written to a temporary file and renamed into place: the name appears only complete.\n    staged = f\"{pidfile}.tmp\"\n    try:\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.CallFailed, match=\"stopped by\"):\n            stage2.launch(\n                [\"bash\", \"-c\", f\"sleep 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > {staged} && mv {staged} {pidfile}; wait\"],\n                tmp_path,\n                {**os.environ},\n                timeout=1,\n                limit=\"the test limit\",\n            )\n        assert handed[0] == 1, \"the step was handed more than its allowance\"\n        assert handed[1] == stage2.KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS, \"the kill's drain is unbounded\"\n        (pid,) = known\n        for _ in range(100):  # watchdog only: the kill is delivered at once, the exit is reaped a moment later\n            if not _child_alive(pid):\n                return\n            time.sleep(0.02)\n        pytest.fail(\"the grandchild of the timed-out step is still running\")\n    finally:\n        # cleanup: every known PID is killed; a missing or already dead one is tolerated\n        _kill_known(known[0] if known else _complete_pid(pidfile))\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_launcher_forces_noninteractive_permissions(workspace: SimpleNamespace) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 2, test half: the launched call and the overlay leave no interactive permission wait.\"\"\"\n    write_settings(\n        user_settings(workspace),\n        {\"statusLine\": {\"type\": \"command\"}, \"permissions\": {\"ask\": [ASK_RULE], \"deny\": [DENY_RULE]}},\n    )\n    write_settings(local_settings(workspace), {\"permissions\": {\"deny\": [\"Bash(rm -rf /)\"]}})\n    passthrough = [\"-p\", \"night work\", \"--model\", \"sonnet\"]\n    done = run_night(workspace, *passthrough)\n    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stderr\n    argv = launched_argv(workspace)\n    assert argv[0] == \"--settings\" and Path(argv[1]).name == \"settings.json\"\n    assert argv[2:4] == [\"--permission-mode\", \"dontAsk\"]\n    assert argv[4:] == passthrough\n    overlay = recorded_overlay(workspace)\n    assert overlay[\"permissions\"][\"defaultMode\"] == \"dontAsk\"\n    assert \"ask\" not in overlay[\"permissions\"]\n    assert \"allow\" not in overlay[\"permissions\"], \"the night profile must not add blanket allows\"\n    deny = overlay[\"permissions\"][\"deny\"]\n    assert len(deny) == len(set(deny)), \"the overlay repeats a deny rule\"\n    assert set(deny) == {ASK_RULE, DENY_RULE, \"Bash(rm -rf /)\"}\n    assert set(overlay) == {\"permissions\"}, \"inherited non-permission settings must stay in their native layers\"\n    assert recorded(workspace, \".lifetime\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"True 0o700\"\n    assert not Path(argv[1]).exists(), \"the overlay outlived the child\"\n    assert not Path(argv[1]).parent.exists(), \"the private overlay directory outlived the child\"\n",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_timeout_kills_the_whole_process_group(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"O188-4: a grandchild of the stopped step does not survive.\"\"\"\n    # Planted fault: a timed-out group's descendant survives, or the post-kill drain is unbounded.\n    pidfile = tmp_path / \"grandchild.pid\"\n    handed: list[float | None] = []  # every timeout a communicate was given, the drain's included\n    known: list[int] = []  # the grandchild's PID once complete, so cleanup can always reach it\n    real_popen = subprocess.Popen\n\n    def popen(command, *args, **kwargs):\n        process = real_popen(command, *args, **kwargs)\n        real_communicate = process.communicate\n\n        def communicate(timeout=None):\n            handed.append(timeout)\n            if len(handed) == 1:\n                # Readiness, not a race: the grandchild's complete PID is held before the expiry is injected.\n                pid = _await_complete_pid(pidfile, 200)\n                assert pid is not None, \"the timed step never wrote its grandchild's complete pid\"\n                known.append(pid)\n                raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(command, timeout)\n            return real_communicate(timeout=timeout)  # the bounded drain on the really killed group\n\n        process.communicate = communicate  # type: ignore[method-assign]\n        return process\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, \"Popen\", popen)\n    # The record is written to a temporary file and renamed into place: the name appears only complete.\n    staged = f\"{pidfile}.tmp\"\n    try:\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.CallFailed, match=\"stopped by\"):\n            stage2.launch(\n                [\"bash\", \"-c\", f\"sleep 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > {staged} && mv {staged} {pidfile}; wait\"],\n                tmp_path,\n                {**os.environ},\n                timeout=1,\n                limit=\"the test limit\",\n            )\n        assert handed[0] == 1, \"the step was handed more than its allowance\"\n        assert handed[1] == stage2.KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS, \"the kill's drain is unbounded\"\n        (pid,) = known\n        for _ in range(100):  # watchdog only: the kill is delivered at once, the exit is reaped a moment later\n            if not _child_alive(pid):\n                return\n            time.sleep(0.02)\n        pytest.fail(\"the grandchild of the timed-out step is still running\")\n    finally:\n        # cleanup: every known PID is killed; a missing or already dead one is tolerated\n        _kill_known(known[0] if known else _complete_pid(pidfile))\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_launcher_forces_noninteractive_permissions(workspace: SimpleNamespace) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 2, test half: the launched call and the overlay leave no interactive permission wait.\"\"\"\n    write_settings(\n        user_settings(workspace),\n        {\"statusLine\": {\"type\": \"command\"}, \"permissions\": {\"ask\": [ASK_RULE], \"deny\": [DENY_RULE]}},\n    )\n    write_settings(local_settings(workspace), {\"permissions\": {\"deny\": [\"Bash(rm -rf /)\"]}})\n    passthrough = [\"-p\", \"night work\", \"--model\", \"sonnet\"]\n    done = run_night(workspace, *passthrough)\n    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stderr\n    argv = launched_argv(workspace)\n    assert argv[0] == \"--settings\" and Path(argv[1]).name == \"settings.json\"\n    assert argv[2:4] == [\"--permission-mode\", \"dontAsk\"]\n    assert argv[4:] == passthrough\n    overlay = recorded_overlay(workspace)\n    assert overlay[\"permissions\"][\"defaultMode\"] == \"dontAsk\"\n    assert \"ask\" not in overlay[\"permissions\"]\n    assert \"allow\" not in overlay[\"permissions\"], \"the night profile must not add blanket allows\"\n    deny = overlay[\"permissions\"][\"deny\"]\n    assert len(deny) == len(set(deny)), \"the overlay repeats a deny rule\"\n    assert set(deny) == {ASK_RULE, DENY_RULE, \"Bash(rm -rf /)\"}\n    assert set(overlay) == {\"permissions\"}, \"inherited non-permission settings must stay in their native layers\"\n    assert recorded(workspace, \".lifetime\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"True 0o700\"\n    assert not Path(argv[1]).exists(), \"the overlay outlived the child\"\n    assert not Path(argv[1]).parent.exists(), \"the private overlay directory outlived the child\"\n",

          "end_line": 8207,
          "excerpt": "def test_a_timeout_kills_the_whole_process_group(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"O188-4: a grandchild of the stopped step does not survive.\"\"\"\n    # Planted fault: a timed-out group's descendant survives, or the post-kill drain is unbounded.\n    pidfile = tmp_path / \"grandchild.pid\"\n    handed: list[float | None] = []  # every timeout a communicate was given, the drain's included\n    known: list[int] = []  # the grandchild's PID once complete, so cleanup can always reach it\n    real_popen = subprocess.Popen\n\n    def popen(command, *args, **kwargs):\n        process = real_popen(command, *args, **kwargs)\n        real_communicate = process.communicate\n\n        def communicate(timeout=None):\n            handed.append(timeout)\n            if len(handed) == 1:\n                # Readiness, not a race: the grandchild's complete PID is held before the expiry is injected.\n                pid = _await_complete_pid(pidfile, 200)\n                assert pid is not None, \"the timed step never wrote its grandchild's complete pid\"\n                known.append(pid)\n                raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(command, timeout)\n            return real_communicate(timeout=timeout)  # the bounded drain on the really killed group\n\n        process.communicate = communicate  # type: ignore[method-assign]\n        return process\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, \"Popen\", popen)\n    # The record is written to a temporary file and renamed into place: the name appears only complete.\n    staged = f\"{pidfile}.tmp\"\n    try:\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.CallFailed, match=\"stopped by\"):\n            stage2.launch(\n                [\"bash\", \"-c\", f\"sleep 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > {staged} && mv {staged} {pidfile}; wait\"],\n                tmp_path,\n                {**os.environ},\n                timeout=1,\n                limit=\"the test limit\",\n            )\n        assert handed[0] == 1, \"the step was handed more than its allowance\"\n        assert handed[1] == stage2.KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS, \"the kill's drain is unbounded\"\n        (pid,) = known\n        for _ in range(100):  # watchdog only: the kill is delivered at once, the exit is reaped a moment later\n            if not _child_alive(pid):\n                return\n            time.sleep(0.02)\n        pytest.fail(\"the grandchild of the timed-out step is still running\")\n    finally:\n        # cleanup: every known PID is killed; a missing or already dead one is tolerated\n        _kill_known(known[0] if known else _complete_pid(pidfile))\n",

          "excerpt": "def _stage2_row(tokens: list[str], pid: str, elapsed: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> ProcessRow | None:\n    script = next((i for i, token in enumerate(tokens) if _is_stage2_script(token)), None)\n    if script is None or script + 1 >= len(tokens) or tokens[script + 1] not in KNOWN_VERBS:\n        return None\n    if script != 0:\n        if not re.fullmatch(r\"python(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*)?\", Path(tokens[0]).name):\n            return None  # the executable owns the invocation, not a preceding argument\n        if any(not token.startswith(\"-\") or token in {\"-c\", \"-m\", \"--\"} for token in tokens[1:script]):\n            return None\n    verb = tokens[script + 1]\n    change = NOT_READ\n    arguments = iter(tokens[script + 2 :])\n    value_options = {\n        \"--model\",\n        \"--class\",\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        \"--seats\",\n        \"--handover\",\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        \"--reason\",\n        \"--root\",\n    }\n    for token in arguments:\n        if token == \"--stage2-off\":\n            # Its reason is optional. A known change or another option must\n            # remain available to the positional/option reader below.\n            following = next(arguments, None)\n            if following is None:\n                break\n            if following not in changes and not following.startswith(\"-\"):\n                continue  # the explicit reason\n            token = following\n        if token in value_options:\n            next(arguments, None)\n            continue\n        if token.startswith(\"-\"):\n            continue  # options may stand between the verb and the change\n        if token in changes:\n            change = token\n        break  # only the first non-option token can name the change\n    return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=verb, change=change)\n",

          "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        elif not table:\n            raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        for line in table:\n            parts = line.split(None, 2)\n            if (\n                len(parts) != 3\n                or not parts[0].isdigit()\n                or not run_report.ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1])\n                or not parts[2].strip()\n            ):\n                raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        rows = run_report.parse_processes(raw, changes)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        lines.append(str(error))\n        return lines\n    if not rows:\n        if run_report.stage2 is not None:\n            lines.append(\"none matched\")\n        return lines\n  ",

          "excerpt": "def holding_key(key: str) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"One runner per loop record at a time (R-14 of the review-swarm review), by the record's key.\n\n    Two runners that both read `consumed: []` pay the same members and number the same round twice,\n    and the doubled ids then block `repair`. The lock is advisory, held by the open descriptor, and\n    a descriptor dies with its process - so a crashed run leaves no lock behind to break the next.\n    Supersession holds its own and every selected worktree's lock in one deterministic order, so it\n    cannot bypass a normal user of either record (bead coding-harness-e82i, criterion 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    path = record_base() / f\"{key}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"another run holds the loop record `{key}`; one runner at a time\") from error\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "excerpt": "def state_base() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"The state base the shared root hangs off; an inheriting child must keep this, not the root.\n\n    A child handed `XDG_STATE_HOME` pointing at the root itself would resolve\n    the next layer down (`.../coding-harness/coding-harness`) and read another\n    machine's state — so the environment a local child inherits names the base,\n    and both sides resolve the same root.\n    \"\"\"\n    base = os.environ.get(\"XDG_STATE_HOME\")\n    # A relative value is ignored, as the XDG base-directory rule says: it would resolve against each\n    # entry's own working directory and split the shared admission (review row L1-3).\n    return Path(base) if base and Path(base).is_absolute() else Path.home() / \".local\" / \"state\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def inherit_env(env: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The environment a local check runs under, with the admission state it must carry.\n\n    This is additive and local-only: a runner's allowlist stays closed, foreign\n    calls receive none of these names, and a genuine inherited marker travels\n    so a nested check reuses its ancestor's admission even after local\n    environment filtering.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = dict(env)\n    env[\"XDG_STATE_HOME\"] = str(state_base())\n    if FLOOR_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[FLOOR_ENV] = os.environ[FLOOR_ENV]\n    # The slot setting travels to local children when present, so a nested\n    # runner's own protected work — never a nested entry, which parses\n    # nothing — sees the same configuration its parent had (criterion 2).\n    # The foreign-model environment allowlist stays closed to HARNESS_*.\n    if SLOTS_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[SLOTS_ENV] = os.environ[SLOTS_ENV]\n    nested = nested_holder_pid()\n    marker, token = (nested, os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV)) if nested is not None else (_active_pid(), _active_token())\n    if marker is not None and token:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(marker)\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = token\n    else:\n        env.pop(LOCK_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(TOKEN_ENV, None)\n    # The admission context resolves the same way the child itself would: its\n    # own active admission, an inherited one, or nothing (bead\n    # coding-harness-1um6). A fresh context travels so the child records the\n    # measured wait as its own; an inherited one does not travel — the child\n    # resolves the shared context from the validated ownership record instead.\n    # Never the token.\n    context = admission_context()\n    if context.admission_id is not None and context.reused is False:\n        env[ADMISSION_ID_ENV] = context.admission_id\n        if context.wait_seconds is not None:\n            env[ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV] = repr(context.wait_seconds)\n    else:\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_ID_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(ADMISSION_WAIT_ENV, None)\n    return env\n",

      "statement": "Every runner job today is a child of the orchestrating session: launch() starts each timed program in its own session but registers its process group in the runner's in-memory _LIVE_GROUPS set, and kill_live() SIGKILLs every registered group when the runner is interrupted or terminated; the 2026-11-05 addendum records six runner jobs that most likely stopped when their session ended. A detached job therefore faces a two-sided risk: if it stays registered under the runner's launch path, any interrupted runner ends it — the exact coupling the change removes; if it escapes registration, no read code path kills or reaps it after its launcher dies, and its group membership lives only in the launcher's memory."

          "excerpt": "def _stage2_row(tokens: list[str], pid: str, elapsed: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> ProcessRow | None:\n    script = next((i for i, token in enumerate(tokens) if _is_stage2_script(token)), None)\n    if script is None or script + 1 >= len(tokens) or tokens[script + 1] not in KNOWN_VERBS:\n        return None\n    if script != 0:\n        if not re.fullmatch(r\"python(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*)?\", Path(tokens[0]).name):\n            return None  # the executable owns the invocation, not a preceding argument\n        if any(not token.startswith(\"-\") or token in {\"-c\", \"-m\", \"--\"} for token in tokens[1:script]):\n            return None\n    verb = tokens[script + 1]\n    change = NOT_READ\n    arguments = iter(tokens[script + 2 :])\n    value_options = {\n        \"--model\",\n        \"--class\",\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        \"--seats\",\n        \"--handover\",\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        \"--reason\",\n        \"--root\",\n    }\n    for token in arguments:\n        if token == \"--stage2-off\":\n            # Its reason is optional. A known change or another option must\n            # remain available to the positional/option reader below.\n            following = next(arguments, None)\n            if following is None:\n                break\n            if following not in changes and not following.startswith(\"-\"):\n                continue  # the explicit reason\n            token = following\n        if token in value_options:\n            next(arguments, None)\n            continue\n        if token.startswith(\"-\"):\n            continue  # options may stand between the verb and the change\n        if token in changes:\n            change = token\n        break  # only the first non-option token can name the change\n    return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=verb, change=change)\n",

          "excerpt": "def inherit_env(env: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The environment a local check runs under, with the admission state it must carry.\n\n    This is additive and local-only: a runner's allowlist stays closed, foreign\n    calls receive none of these names, and a genuine inherited marker travels\n    so a nested check reuses its ancestor's admission even after local\n    environment filtering.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = dict(env)\n    env[\"XDG_STATE_HOME\"] = str(state_base())\n    if FLOOR_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[FLOOR_ENV] = os.environ[FLOOR_ENV]\n    # The slot setting travels to local children when present, so a nested\n    # runner's own protected work — never a nested entry, which parses\n    # nothing — sees the same configuration its parent had (criterion 2).\n    # The foreign-model environment allowlist stays closed to HARNESS_*.\n    if SLOTS_ENV in os.environ:\n        env[SLOTS_ENV] = os.environ[SLOTS_ENV]\n    nested = nested_holder_pid()\n    marker, token = (nested, os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV)) if nested is not None else (_active_pid(), _active_token())\n    if marker is not None and token:\n        env[LOCK_ENV] = str(marker)\n        env[TOKEN_ENV] = token\n    else:\n        env.pop(LOCK_ENV, None)\n        env.pop(TOKEN_ENV, None)\n    # The admission context resolves the same way the child itself would: its\n    # own active admission, an inherited one, or nothing (bead\n    # coding-harness-1um6).
